method: Source delta audit against immutable v0.9.15 and v0.9.20 trees (v0.9.16 and v0.9.18 were tagged but never published; changes are labelled with the first published release that contains them); carried citations remapped through identical source text, changed paths inspected for observable semantics. Hosted all-profile Lab evidence is recorded in the audit; no completeness claim. See docs/audit/gateway-0.9.20-delta.md.

headers.name: X-Gateway-Error
headers.writer: src/proxy/mod.rs:28709 x_gateway_error_for_response and final authoritative builders; src/http3/server.rs:12549 finalize_h3_response_gateway_headers; src/proxy/headers.rs:1200 gateway-owned strip list; src/plugins/adaptive_concurrency.rs:27; src/proxy/mod.rs:34851 proxy_hop_limit_refusal_response; src/proxy/mod.rs:349 LOOP_DETECTED_REJECT_HEADERS
headers.semantics: Closed 9-token vocabulary (src/retry.rs:212-257, list at :247): connection_failure, backend_timeout, request_timeout, backend_error, circuit_breaker_open, overload, config_stale, concurrency_limit, loop_detected (v0.9.17, #6127). On backend-dispatch responses derived from (connection_error, final status): connection_error -> connection_failure; status 504 -> backend_timeout; status >=500 -> backend_error; else absent (src/retry.rs:301). Two overrides (src/proxy/mod.rs:28709 x_gateway_error_for_response): overload on the response-transformer output-ceiling 502, and request_timeout (new in v0.9.8, #5762) on the route-deadline 504 {"error":"Request timeout"} when the recorded route-timeout phase is not dispatch (before_dispatch, retry_backoff, or an HTTP/3 upload still being buffered): no backend held the request. backend_timeout means the backend dispatch attempt did not answer before its deadline; a route-total expiry after dispatch began counts even while TCP/TLS setup is still in progress, so it does not prove a backend received the request (docs/error_classification.md:507, :519; #6073 docs). Never on 2xx/3xx/4xx from the gateway core; never on native-gRPC trailers-only siblings of the overload/config_stale fences. v0.9.8 writes the token on every HTTP/3 response path (native and bridged, buffered and streamed) and on the H1/H2 native gRPC builders after the last response hook (#5783, #5798, #5807), so a backend 5xx relayed over HTTP/3 or by a gRPC backend now reads backend_error. v0.9.13 (#6008): the same request_timeout 504 also ends an early (pre-before_proxy) body collection bounded by a previewed route total (src/proxy/mod.rs:33088). v0.9.14 (#6022): a reqwest read timeout while buffering a larger or limited response is 504 backend_timeout; other buffered read errors are 502 backend_error. No token, spelling or class-to-token mapping changed. v0.9.15: src/retry.rs is byte-identical; the new route_protocol_admission 403 (gateway.routing.protocol_not_permitted) carries no token because token_for_rejection_phase maps that phase to none, and the WebSocket non-GET 405 carries none either. v0.9.17 (#6127): the hop-limit 508 {"error":"Proxy hop limit exceeded"} carries loop_detected (src/proxy/mod.rs:34881; HTTP/3 src/http3/server.rs:20805 via loop_detected_reject_headers); native gRPC gets FAILED_PRECONDITION without a token; an outer Ferrum hop relaying that 508 writes backend_error and never retries it (src/retry.rs:2006). v0.9.19 (#6777): a backend connect timeout is 504 Backend timeout with connection_failure (connection_error wins over status in src/retry.rs:301), and DestinationRule maxConnections refusals are 503 Backend connection limit exceeded with connection_failure on every transport. No other token, spelling or mapping changed; plugin reject maps are still not stripped.
headers.spoofing_notes: Hardened in v0.9.8 (#5759): X-Gateway-Error and X-Gateway-Upstream-Status (and, from v0.9.9, X-Ferrum-Diagnostic-Ref) are one gateway-owned list (src/proxy/headers.rs:1200 GATEWAY_OWNED_DIAGNOSTIC_RESPONSE_HEADERS); every backend response boundary strips a backend copy in headers or trailers (src/proxy/headers.rs:1157 is_backend_response_strip_header: reqwest, direct HTTP/2, native gRPC, native HTTP/3, the HTTP/3 bridge, serverless functions), and the H1/H2 builder, the native gRPC builders and every HTTP/3 response replace a hook- or plugin-written copy with the gateway's own value. Still NOT stripped from plugin reject header maps (only the adaptive_concurrency and CB/transformer paths restore it authoritatively), so an operator/custom plugin or reject-path header decorator can emit any value on a gateway rejection (lab GW-019 reject-decorated), and any non-Ferrum endpoint can send it. The gateway's own CHANGELOG says the headers are still unauthenticated.

headers.name: X-Gateway-Upstream-Status
headers.writer: src/proxy/mod.rs:46477 (builder .header when upstream_is_fallback, after the :46460 strip); src/http3/server.rs:12494-12510 (finalize_h3_response_routing_headers: strip on every response, insert only when is_fallback)
headers.semantics: Only value 'degraded': load balancer used the all-unhealthy (or unhealthy-subset -> parent) fallback. May accompany any status including 2xx.
headers.spoofing_notes: v0.9.8 (#5759): a backend- or hook-written copy is stripped on the H1/H2 backend-response builder (src/proxy/mod.rs:46460) and on every HTTP/3 response (src/http3/server.rs:12500), so on those paths only the gateway's own 'degraded' reaches the client and never twice. Plugin reject paths do not strip it, and any non-Ferrum endpoint can send it.

headers.name: gateway-error-reason
headers.writer: src/proxy/mod.rs:4026 (backend_tls_sni_requires_direct_h2), :44400/:44472/:44524/:49560 (mesh dispatch); src/http3/server.rs and src/http3/cross_protocol.rs mesh/egress refusal builders; src/http3/websocket.rs:1012
headers.semantics: Undocumented gateway-authored reason on some DispatchPolicyRejected 502s. Values seen: 'backend_tls_sni_requires_direct_h2', 'backend-egress-policy-denied' (H3 bridge only), mesh reasons such as 'mesh transport dispatch required for this backend target', 'Unix socket retry dispatch is unavailable', 'HBONE transport or gateway identity is unavailable for retry target'.
headers.spoofing_notes: Not in any strip list (src/proxy/headers.rs:1157 is_backend_response_strip_header).

headers.name: Via
headers.writer: src/proxy/mod.rs:8009 via_header_for_backend_response_body; src/proxy/mod.rs backend-response builder; src/http3/server.rs:12494 finalize_h3_response_routing_headers
headers.semantics: '1.1 ferrum-edge' / '2.0 ferrum-edge' / '3.0 ferrum-edge' (protocol of the upstream response). Written on responses that pass through the backend-response builder, including gateway-synthesized 502/504 backend failures (buffered => '1.1 <pseudonym>'); NOT written on pre-dispatch gateway rejections built by build_response / build_response_from_normalized_reject (404, 401, 405, 431, 503 overload/config_stale, CB 503). Backend Via hops are retained and the gateway hop appended. v0.9.11: streamed direct-H1, Unix-socket and HBONE inner HTTP/1.1 responses use their actual HTTP/1.1 version (previously the StreamingH2 arm gave Unix/HBONE HTTP/2 Via). Still only a correlation/protocol hint, never proof of origin. v0.9.19 (#6777): FERRUM_VIA_PSEUDONYM must be an RFC 9110 token (optionally :<port>) and is validated at startup.
headers.spoofing_notes: A backend can send 'Via: 1.1 ferrum-edge' itself; operators can rename or disable it.

headers.name: Alt-Svc
headers.writer: src/proxy/mod.rs:46487 via ProxyState::alt_svc_for_frontend_port (src/proxy/mod.rs:11714; value 'h3=":<FERRUM_PROXY_HTTPS_PORT>"; ma=86400' when HTTP/3 enabled)
headers.semantics: Advertises HTTP/3 on backend-path responses when enable_http3. v0.9.7 withheld it on frontend ports serving a route rule with request/attempt timeouts; v0.9.8 enforces those timeouts on native HTTP/3 and advertises HTTP/3 on those ports again (#5646, #5729; RouteTimeoutAltSvc removed).
headers.spoofing_notes: Backend alt-svc is not stripped; gateway value is appended.

headers.name: Allow
headers.writer: src/proxy/mod.rs:28653 restore_authoritative_allow_header (route 405); src/proxy/mod.rs:28691 PROTOCOL_LEVEL_405_ALLOW (TRACE/CONNECT 405); src/proxy/mod.rs:56341 build_method_not_allowed_response_with_allow (Allow: GET on the HTTP/1.1 WebSocket non-GET 405, v0.9.15)
headers.semantics: Route 405: route allowed_methods uppercased, ', '-joined, config order. Protocol 405: 'GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS'. v0.9.15 (#6080): a non-GET HTTP/1.1 WebSocket upgrade gets 405 with Allow: GET (gateway.routing.websocket_upgrade_requires_get).
headers.spoofing_notes: Only on gateway-built 405s; policy cannot alter it. A backend's own 405 Allow passes through untouched.

headers.name: Connection: close
headers.writer: src/proxy/mod.rs:46529 (drain / keepalive pressure / RED shedding on any response); src/proxy/mod.rs:34926 (framing observer 400); src/proxy/mod.rs:34742 (retired-listener 421, every flavor from v0.9.20); src/proxy/h1_framing_guard.rs:82-84 (parse envelopes)
headers.semantics: HTTP/1.1 only. On ordinary responses indicates gateway drain or overload pressure (probabilistic under RED), not an error.
headers.spoofing_notes: Hop-by-hop; backend Connection header is stripped (src/proxy/headers.rs:1149) so a close seen by the client comes from the gateway or an intermediary.

headers.name: x-adaptive-concurrency-limit / x-adaptive-concurrency-inflight
headers.semantics: Only when the adaptive_concurrency plugin has expose_headers enabled and a TargetLimit rejection occurs.
headers.spoofing_notes: Plain names, not stripped from backend responses.

headers.name: WWW-Authenticate
headers.writer: src/plugins/utils/auth_flow.rs:681 auth_rejection (401 + mechanism challenge); src/proxy/mod.rs:33347 missing_authentication_reject; src/proxy/mod.rs:33475 ensure_unauthorized_response_challenge (repairs any gateway/plugin 401 lacking a well-formed challenge); src/plugins/basic_auth.rs:231; src/plugins/ldap_auth.rs:140; src/plugins/oauth2_introspection.rs:1624; src/proxy/mod.rs:56285 (client trust withdrawn); src/proxy/mod.rs:59261 (authorization expiry)
headers.semantics: v0.9.19 (#6779, issue #6774): on every gateway-generated 401. Values: 'ApiKey realm="ferrum-edge"' (key_auth), 'Bearer' / 'Bearer error="invalid_request"' / 'Bearer error="invalid_token"' (jwt_auth, jwks_auth, oauth2_introspection), 'DPoP' / 'DPoP error="invalid_dpop_proof"' / 'DPoP error="invalid_token"' (jwks_auth), 'hmac realm="ferrum-edge"' (hmac_auth), 'Basic realm="ferrum-edge", charset="UTF-8"' (basic_auth, ldap_auth), 'ClientCertificate realm="ferrum-edge"' (mtls_auth, client-trust withdrawal), 'WS-Security realm="ferrum-edge"' (soap_ws_security), 'Bearer realm="oidc"' / 'Bearer realm="oidc", error="invalid_token"' (oidc_relying_party). An authentication-phase 401 lists every rejecting and applicable mechanism's challenge in one field joined by ', '; the literal 'ferrum-edge' is used only when no applicable mechanism advertises one (src/plugins/utils/auth_flow.rs:610). Origin-authored 401s (backend, cache/dedup replays, serverless, federated providers) pass through untouched. Through v0.9.15: On 401 only. Values seen: 'Basic realm="ferrum-edge", charset="UTF-8"' (basic_auth, ldap_auth), 'Bearer' (oauth2_introspection), and the literal fallback 'ferrum-edge' when no credential was presented and no applicable mechanism advertises a challenge (body {"error":"Authentication required"}). DPoP/jwks challenges: see plugin outcomes.
headers.spoofing_notes: Backend WWW-Authenticate passes through on proxied 401s; realm ferrum-edge / bare 'ferrum-edge' is a strong but forgeable Ferrum-like marker.

headers.name: x-request-id (request id)
headers.writer: src/plugins/correlation_id.rs:119 (default header_name), :137 (echo_downstream default true), :412 (applies_after_proxy_on_reject); src/proxy/mod.rs:36429 (global policy on route-miss 404)
headers.semantics: No request-id header is emitted by the gateway core. Only when the correlation_id plugin is enabled on the route: header x-request-id by default (configurable header_name), echoed on responses including plugin rejections by default. Accepts an incoming value from the client if present (not audited in detail). v0.9.19: inbound_policy preserve (default, keeps a well-formed client value) or generate (always mints a UUID v4) (#6876); a GLOBAL correlation_id also decorates unmatched-route 404s on HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 (#6938). x-geo-country and x-real-ip are refused as header_name.
headers.spoofing_notes: Only a correlation aid; not a provenance or authorization token.

headers.name: Content-Type: application/json
headers.semantics: All gateway JSON errors use {"error":"..."} bodies (some add "limit" or "message"). Not a Ferrum identifier by itself. Exception: the backend-failure bodies built by the backend-dispatch builders (502 Backend unavailable / Backend DNS resolution failed / Backend response body read failed / Backend response body exceeds maximum size, 503 Response buffering capacity exceeded / Backend connection limit exceeded, 504 Backend timeout, and the route-deadline 504 Request timeout) carry no Content-Type header on the HTTP/1.1 / HTTP/2 path (empty header map; lab-observed over HTTP/1.1 on 0.9.5 and 0.9.7). Plugin rejects and admission fences do carry application/json. v0.9.19 (#6777): a response the builder rejects falls back to internal_error_fallback_response (src/proxy/mod.rs:56296): 500 with application/json (text/plain for a non-JSON body), never Response::new's 200.

headers.name: grpc-status / grpc-message (gateway-generated)
headers.semantics: Trailers-Only HTTP 200, content-type application/grpc, empty body. HTTP reject status mapped by src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:3132. v0.9.19/v0.9.20 (#6940, #6965): H1/H2 pre-routing refusals answer native gRPC Trailers-Only with fixed messages (pre_routing_refusal_response, src/proxy/mod.rs:34784) and gRPC-Web with framed trailers; the hop-limit refusal uses FAILED_PRECONDITION / INVALID_ARGUMENT.
headers.spoofing_notes: Backends legitimately send grpc-status; no provenance marker distinguishes gateway-authored gRPC errors.

headers.name: Server
headers.semantics: Ferrum sets no Server header (no writer found in src/proxy or src/http3); a Server header seen by the client is the backend's or an intermediary's.

headers.name: X-Ferrum-Diagnostic-Ref
headers.writer: src/diagnostic_ref.rs:1695 stamp_response_headers (the last step before the response head; name at src/diagnostic_ref.rs:82); backend copies stripped with the gateway-owned list (src/proxy/headers.rs:1200), plugin copies at the final client boundary (src/diagnostic_ref.rs:1674 strip_response_header)
headers.semantics: New in v0.9.9 (#5767; PRs #5845, #5857, #5862, #5868). Opaque reference fd1_<32 hex> (fd2_<8 hex replica>_<32 hex> with FERRUM_DIAGNOSTIC_REF_REPLICA_TAG=true): 128 random bits with no embedded cause, route, backend or tenant. FERRUM_DIAGNOSTIC_REFS=off (default) sends none; errors marks the responses that carry the gateway's own X-Gateway-Error; all adds plugin rejections, gateway policy fences and routing 404s (gRPC trailers-only included). A backend's own error response, relayed or replayed by a plugin, never gets one (#5860, PR #5862). The detail (ferrum.diagnostic_ref.v1) is only available from the admin GET /diagnostics/v1/refs/{ref} with a diagnostics:read scope and an ns claim, on the process that minted it.
headers.spoofing_notes: Gateway-owned whatever FERRUM_DIAGNOSTIC_REFS says: a backend or serverless-function copy, in headers or trailers, is stripped at every backend response boundary, and a plugin- or hook-written copy at the final client boundary. A non-Ferrum endpoint can still send the header; only a successful authenticated lookup proves a reference is the gateway's. Anvil uses it only through a trusted profile's lookup, and only a record that binds to the response (docs/diagnostics.md, G01).

headers.name: X-Ferrum-Hops
headers.writer: src/proxy/hop_limit.rs:242 stamp_proxy_hops (frontend, before plugins; re-asserted after every request-phase plugin pass); src/proxy/hop_limit.rs:297 stamp_plugin_call_proxy_hops (request-scoped plugin calls, #6132)
headers.semantics: REQUEST header only, never on client responses. New in v0.9.17 (#6127). Each Ferrum hop forwards received+1 (absent = 0) to the backend on every HTTP-family transport; FERRUM_MAX_PROXY_HOPS (default 10, 0 disables) bounds it with 508 loop_detected; a malformed or repeated value is 400 Invalid X-Ferrum-Hops header. A client may only raise it. A Connection nomination cannot remove it (src/proxy/headers.rs:521). An echo backend therefore sees a Ferrum fingerprint.
headers.spoofing_notes: Clients can send it (only to raise the count or get refused); backends never see the client's value. Not a response marker.

headers.name: X-Ferrum-*
headers.semantics: X-Ferrum-* names in the source are admin-API (e.g. X-Ferrum-Namespace-Unserved, src/admin/mod.rs:2548), internal plugin handoff markers stripped before the wire (x-ferrum-original-content-encoding, grpc-web bridge markers), or mesh request markers. None is a client-facing proxy response header at v0.9.8; v0.9.9 adds X-Ferrum-Diagnostic-Ref (its own entry). Also the mesh-only x-ferrum-mesh-tunnel-reuse: fenced on an HBONE CONNECT 200 (v0.9.6+, src/proxy/hbone_proxy.rs:1743, name at src/modes/mesh/hbone.rs:47), which only a peer mesh proxy sees; it advertises a capability and is not a diagnostic marker. v0.9.17 adds x-ferrum-hops, a gateway-owned REQUEST header backends see (own entry); still no X-Ferrum-* response header besides X-Ferrum-Diagnostic-Ref.

headers.name: Content-Security-Policy
headers.semantics: v0.9.6+ (released v0.9.7): "default-src 'none'; sandbox" on spec documents served by spec_expose (also on HEAD); not on its fetch-error responses. Not a diagnostic marker.
headers.spoofing_notes: Any backend can send a Content-Security-Policy on its own responses; only its presence on a spec_expose document is gateway-authored.

error_class_semantics.typical_http: 502 Backend DNS resolution failed (shared preflight before reqwest/direct-H1) or Backend unavailable (later pooled DNS failures)

error_class_semantics.note: TlsError only on independent setup-phase evidence; a rustls error surfacing after reqwest's TCP-only connect is connection_reset (issue #4536). Doc-only change in v0.9.19 (#6732).

error_class_semantics.typical_http: 499 log/metrics only (gRPC CANCELLED) on proven client abort on every protocol; 408 body read timeout; 400 Malformed request body (mesh/HBONE/Unix dispatch, H3 log-only); auth-expiry 401 placeholder
502 Backend response body exceeds maximum size
502 Backend unavailable (H3 pre-header) / WS normal close

error_class_semantics.x_gateway_error_typical: backend_error (overload for the transformer ceiling; request_timeout for a route-deadline 504 no backend held)
connection_failure (pools); reqwest admission refusal keeps its dispatch_policy_rejected class
error_class_semantics.typical_http: 503 {"error":"Backend connection limit exceeded"} on direct H2, native H3, HBONE, sidecar mTLS and the reqwest lane (v0.9.19, #6771; pools were 502 Backend unavailable)

grpc_reject_status_mapping.note: Gateway-generated native-gRPC rejects are HTTP 200 Trailers-Only (content-type application/grpc, grpc-status, grpc-message); grpc-message comes from the reject header, else the JSON body's grpc_message/message/error/details field (mod.rs:25841). v0.9.17 (#6146): 499 maps to CANCELLED (src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:3150). The hop-limit 508 does not use this table (explicit FAILED_PRECONDITION 9); a plugin 508 would fall to the default 13.

rejection_phases_operator_only.note: rejection_phase is transaction-log metadata only (never a response header). Values found in log_*rejected_request call sites of src/proxy/mod.rs and src/http3/*.rs; token_for_rejection_phase (src/retry.rs:340) maps circuit_breaker_open|circuit_breaker|adaptive_concurrency|overload|config_stale to metric tokens. v0.9.8: route_request_timeout_unsupported is gone (native HTTP/3 enforces route timeouts), route_request_timeout_h3_upload is new (src/http3/server.rs:20109), and a relay-synthesis refusal of an inbound HBONE CONNECT now logs the deny policy (hbone_relay_destination_denied, hbone_relay_not_ready, hbone_unauthenticated_peer, or the hbone_udp_* variants; src/proxy/mod.rs:3211) instead of no transaction line. v0.9.9: websocket_permessage_deflate is new (an invalid backend permessage-deflate answer, protocol.ws.backend_extension_negotiation_failed). The diagnostic-reference detail's rejection.phase labels (route_not_found, gateway_listener_retired, backend_admission, …; src/diagnostic_ref.rs) are a separate, admin-only vocabulary. v0.9.13: route_request_timeout_early_upload is new (src/proxy/mod.rs:33079; native HTTP/3 src/http3/server.rs:20009), logged when a previewed route total ends an early body collection. v0.9.14: native-H3 dispatch-stage 413 and both bridge drain refusals now log on_final_request_body and run the reject-path hooks. v0.9.15: route_protocol_admission is new (src/diagnostic_ref.rs:200 ROUTE_PROTOCOL_ADMISSION_PHASE; src/proxy/mod.rs:36683, native HTTP/3 src/http3/server.rs:4434), logged when a native gRPC or WebSocket request is refused because its flavor view omits the route's authentication or admission policy; token_for_rejection_phase maps it to no token. The HTTP/3 CONNECT-UDP per-client cap logs connect_udp_per_ip_session_limit (src/http3/connect_udp.rs:2106). v0.9.17 (#6127): proxy_hop_limit and proxy_hops_invalid are gateway rejection phases (src/diagnostic_ref.rs:234-235) recorded only in the diagnostic reference (rejection.phase); the fence emits no transaction summary. token_for_rejection_phase maps proxy_hop_limit to loop_detected (src/retry.rs:346) and proxy_hops_invalid to none. v0.9.17/v0.9.19: client_disconnect_* upload phases (#6146, #6150) and the ClientAbortScope phases (#6781: 499 client_disconnect_before_response, 400 protocol_error_before_response, 444 gateway_close_* / connection_closed_before_response). v0.9.19 (#6690): query_trigger_admission (src/diagnostic_ref.rs:204). Statuses 499 and 444 are log vocabulary only.

matrix_seed_reconciliation.source: Historical seed coverage from the v0.9.5..v0.9.15 audits, carried with the v0.9.15 -> v0.9.20 source delta recorded in docs/audit/gateway-0.9.20-delta.md; hosted scenario counts recorded in the qualification evidence there.

notes.dns_lookup_error/UP-001: public body is path-dependent: reqwest preflight 'Backend DNS resolution failed' vs pools 'Backend unavailable'
notes.tls_error/UP-004,UP-006: backend mTLS on the reqwest HTTP/1 pool surfaces as connection_pool_error (connection_failure) or connection_reset (backend_error), not tls_error
notes.read_write_timeout/UP-009..011: identical public 504 pair; streamed UP-011 is a truncated body, not a 504
notes.connection_pool_error/UP-016: v0.9.7 and v0.9.8: the stranded pooled HTTP/1 request race of v0.9.5 is fixed (hyper-util patch carried to 0.1.21); a fresh connection fails at once as 502 connection_failure (connection_pool_error, upstream.pool.dispatch_canceled) and a reused one is replayed transparently, so UP-016 never yields the delayed 504 on this release
notes.backend_connection_limit/UP-018: The retained reqwest lane yields 503 Backend connection limit exceeded + backend_error with dispatch_policy_rejected. The new direct-H1 lane uses the typed pooled backend_connection_limit class, as direct-H2/H3/gRPC/HBONE already do; public signals remain coarse.
notes.graceful_remote_close/PROTO-009: for WebSocket this is a log class only; the client sees the relayed peer Close
notes.config_stale/GW-005: requires DP mode, lost CP, age > FERRUM_DP_CONFIG_MAX_STALE_SECONDS (3600) and FERRUM_DP_CONFIG_STALE_ACTION=fail_closed; readiness_only produces no client signal
notes.overload/GW-002,GW-003,GW-009: overload and drain are byte-identical; GW-009 is 502 with {error,limit} body

marker_semantics.note: Release-specific sentences Anvil adds to its marker findings (ferrum.token.<token>, ferrum.marker.absent) when a trusted profile declares this compatibility id. The wording in catalog/diagnostics/findings.en.json stays release-neutral, so a profile whose compatibility id has no catalog gets only the meaning every audited release shares.

backend_timeout.explanation: On Ferrum Edge 0.9.20 the gateway's backend dispatch attempt did not answer before its deadline: a backend read/write timeout, or a route's total request timeout that expired after dispatch began (even while the TCP/TLS connection was still being set up, so it does not prove a backend received the request). A route total that expires before dispatch carries request_timeout, and a backend connect timeout is a 504 with connection_failure. A backend's own 504 also carries this value.

request_timeout.explanation: On Ferrum Edge 0.9.20 this value means the matched route's total request timeout (Gateway API HTTPRoute timeouts.request) expired before backend dispatch began: while the client upload was still being received, during gateway processing or admission, or while waiting to retry after an earlier failed attempt.

backend_error.explanation: On Ferrum Edge 0.9.20 it is attached to 5xx responses the backend returned itself (over every protocol, including HTTP/3 and gRPC backends, and a 508 relayed from an inner Ferrum hop), to failures the gateway observed talking to the backend after the request was sent, and to some gateway-only refusals (response-buffer capacity, HTTP/1.1 in-flight limits, egress-policy denials, response-phase policy rejections).

loop_detected.explanation: On Ferrum Edge 0.9.20 this value means the gateway that wrote it refused the request with 508 Loop Detected before routing, because the X-Ferrum-Hops count it received had reached its proxy hop limit (FERRUM_MAX_PROXY_HOPS, default 10). Every Ferrum gateway increments that count when it forwards a request, so a routing loop or a long chain of gateways is the usual cause, but the count is a request header a caller or an intermediary can also set. No backend was contacted by the refusing gateway.
alternatives: The caller, or a proxy in front of the gateway, sent or forwarded an X-Ferrum-Hops value at or above the limit.
does_not_prove: How many gateways the request actually passed through.
loop_detected.source: src/retry.rs:229 OBS_LOOP_DETECTED; src/proxy/hop_limit.rs:211 decide_proxy_hops (reads the received header); src/proxy/mod.rs:34851; outcome gateway.admission.proxy_hop_limit

connection_failure.explanation: On Ferrum Edge 0.9.20 the gateway could not get the request onto a backend connection: refused, reset during setup, DNS, TLS setup or pool failure (502), a backend connect timeout (504), or a DestinationRule maxConnections refusal before dialing (503). The request was not sent.
connection_failure.source: src/retry.rs:301 (connection_error wins over status); src/proxy/mod.rs:50117; docs/error_classification.md:506

absent.explanation: On Ferrum Edge 0.9.20 plugin rejections carry no X-Gateway-Error value; nor do gateway client-error refusals such as the malformed X-Ferrum-Hops 400.

removed_outcomes.reason: v0.9.17 (#6150, issue #6022): GrpcRequestBodyCollectError lost its Proxy(GrpcProxyError) variant; the INTERNAL 'Failed to read gRPC request body: {Debug}' arm is gone (no emitter of that text at v0.9.20). outcomes.remediation: Do not auto-retry non-idempotent requests. Gateway operator/API owner: correlate gateway logs (error_class) and backend logs for resets or crashes around this time.
outcomes.notes: Post-wire (request_reached_wire=true): only status-code retries gated by retryable_methods can replay it. No Content-Type header on the HTTP/1.1 / HTTP/2 backend-response path: the gateway builds this body with an empty header map (lab-observed over HTTP/1.1 on 0.9.5 and 0.9.7: UP-002, UP-020, GW-019-ERROR; the v0.9.5 audit had recorded application/json). The HTTP/3 writer was not lab-checked. v0.9.20 (#6979, issue #6976): on the reqwest header wait, a backend failure observed at or after the earlier of the dispatch bound (authorization lifetime / client RPC deadline) and the backend_read_timeout_ms header bound now settles as that bound (src/proxy/mod.rs:59012, call site :52790): a reset or close that lands after backend_read_timeout_ms is answered as the 504 backend_timeout of upstream.timeout.response_header_wait, not this 502. The direct H1 pool does the same at its handoff bound (#6973). v0.9.19 (#6778, issue #6776): on the sidecar mesh-mTLS, HBONE and Unix-socket dispatchers, a reset the gateway itself raised because the client abandoned its upload is no longer this 502: it is 499 client_disconnect (proven client abort) or 400 (malformed or incomplete upload) (src/proxy/mod.rs:56691). A reset, CANCEL or close sent by the backend still ends here.

outcomes.condition: backend_read_timeout_ms (default 30000, src/config/types.rs:6631) expired waiting for response headers after the request was sent.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge reports the upstream did not complete its part of the exchange within the gateway's backend timeout budget; the request may have been partially or fully delivered.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Which direction stalled (upload write vs response header wait vs buffered body idle), that the backend definitely received the full request, or that raising timeouts is the fix.
outcomes.remediation: API owner: check backend latency for this operation; gateway operator: check backend_read_timeout_ms / backend_write_timeout_ms for the route. Retry only idempotent requests.
outcomes.notes: post-wire class; not replayed by retry_on_connect_failure. From v0.9.6 the pooled HTTP/1 stranded-request race no longer ends here (it is replayed or fails fast as upstream.pool.dispatch_canceled). Gateway API timeouts.backendRequest also sets the rule's timeout_ms (src/config_sources/k8s/gateway_api.rs:7581), which bounds this same wait. On Unix-socket HTTP/1 backends the read window is one absolute instant across the at-most-once idle-race replay (src/proxy/mod.rs:61873). No Content-Type header on the HTTP/1.1 / HTTP/2 backend-response path: the gateway builds this body with an empty header map (lab-observed over HTTP/1.1 on 0.9.5 and 0.9.7: UP-009, UP-010; the v0.9.5 audit had recorded application/json). The HTTP/3 writer was not lab-checked. v0.9.20 (#6979, issue #6976): a reqwest header wait now also ends here when a backend failure (reset, close) is observed at or after backend_read_timeout_ms and that bound is earlier than any dispatch bound; the response-header bound wins an exact tie (src/proxy/mod.rs:59012, :52796). v0.9.19 (#6777): a backend connect timeout now answers the same 504 {"error":"Backend timeout"} but with X-Gateway-Error connection_failure (upstream.connect.timeout); a post-wire native-H3 (QUIC) connection timeout gives exactly this signal, with error_class connection_timeout.

outcomes.condition: backend_write_timeout_ms (default 30000, src/config/types.rs:6635) watermark expired while the backend stopped reading the request body (upload pump), before response headers.

The HTTP/3 writer was not lab-checked. v0.9.11: Unlimited unauthenticated direct-H2 uploads now enforce backend_write_timeout_ms in Hyper. Before headers the same 504/backend_timeout/read_write_timeout applies; after headers the upload stall resets the stream. Slow frontend input is not a backend write stall; zero disables the write bound. v0.9.19 (#6788): on the Sidecar mesh-mTLS (and h2c Unix-socket) HTTP/2 dispatcher, an upload without an authorization lifetime is bounded by hyper's HTTP/2 body pipe (Http2BodyWriteTimeout, src/proxy/mod.rs:63421) instead of the upload pump. Before headers it ends with the same 504 / read_write_timeout (gRPC DEADLINE_EXCEEDED); after headers the stream is reset. Mesh only; signal unchanged.

outcomes.condition: Response headers arrived on the reqwest path with a trusted Content-Length <= FERRUM_RESPONSE_BUFFER_CUTOFF_BYTES (default 65536, src/config/env_config.rs:5335) and not an event-stream, so the gateway eagerly buffers it; the body read then failed with a non-timeout error (reset, FIN before Content-Length). The backend status is replaced.

public_signal.transport: complete HTTP response replacing backend status

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge received response headers from the upstream but the response body could not be read completely; the backend may have processed the request.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend returned 502, or that the request was not processed.
outcomes.remediation: API owner: check backend for crashes/resets mid-response; do not auto-retry non-idempotent requests.
outcomes.notes: error_class is whatever classify_reqwest_error returns (connection_closed / connection_reset / protocol_error / request_error); pre-wire classes are coerced to connection_reset. No Content-Type header on the HTTP/1.1 / HTTP/2 backend-response path: the gateway builds this body with an empty header map (lab-observed over HTTP/1.1 on 0.9.5 and 0.9.7: UP-013; the v0.9.5 audit had recorded application/json). The HTTP/3 writer was not lab-checked. v0.9.14 (#6022): the buffered collector for larger or limited responses now returns this exact status, body and class (upstream.body_read_failed.buffered_collector), so the body no longer identifies the eager path. A typed backend HTTP/2 reset during the read is protocol_error (was request_error).

outcomes.condition: Buffered collection of a larger or size-limited reqwest response (collect_response_with_limit, above the eager cutoff or under a response size limit) hits a mid-body read error that is not a timeout; status and class follow the eager collector (eager_buffer_body_read_status_and_class).

public_signal.transport: complete HTTP response replacing backend status

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge received response headers from the upstream but failed while reading the response body; the backend may have processed the request.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the body was too large, which collector failed, or that the backend returned 502.
outcomes.remediation: API owner: check backend for mid-response failures.
outcomes.notes: v0.9.14 (#6022): BufferedCollectFailure::read_error classifies through classify_reqwest_error exactly as the eager collector does, so the class is real (connection_closed / connection_reset / protocol_error / request_error; pre-wire classes coerce to connection_reset) and the body is the eager collector's (src/proxy/mod.rs:50213). Earlier releases answered 502 {"error":"Backend response read error"} and logged response_body_too_large; that body no longer exists in v0.9.14 source. A reqwest-reported read timeout is 504 {"error":"Backend timeout"} / backend_timeout / read_write_timeout, the same signal as the collector's own idle timeout. These 502s can now be replayed under retryable_status_codes for a retryable method. The failure response is built with an empty header map (src/proxy/mod.rs:48906: no Content-Type; the 0.9.11 catalog's application/json is not carried). Identical public signal to upstream.body_read_failed.eager_buffer.

outcomes.condition: Backend Content-Length exceeds the effective max response body size (FERRUM_MAX_RESPONSE_BODY_SIZE_BYTES default 10485760, or route response_size_limiting), or a buffered body grows past it.

public_signal.transport: complete HTTP response replacing backend status

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the upstream response because it exceeds the gateway's configured response size limit.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend crashed or returned 502.
outcomes.remediation: API owner: page or reduce the response; gateway operator: review the response size limit for this route.
outcomes.notes: gRPC buffered path maps ResponseTooLarge through the gRPC trailers-only mapping (see protocol outcomes). Streaming without Content-Length is enforced mid-stream instead (streaming.response_size_exceeded_mid_stream). No Content-Type header on the HTTP/1.1 / HTTP/2 backend-response path: the gateway builds this body with an empty header map (lab-observed over HTTP/1.1 on 0.9.5 and 0.9.7: UP-014; the v0.9.5 audit had recorded application/json). The HTTP/3 writer was not lab-checked. v0.9.8 (#5804, #5805, #5807): the HTTP/3 declared-oversize 502 (native streaming relays and the bridge) and the bridge's buffered body-collection refusals now carry X-Gateway-Error: backend_error, as on HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2; v0.9.7 sent them over HTTP/3 without a token.

outcomes.condition: Process-wide retained-response budget (FERRUM_RESPONSE_BUFFER_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES, default 256 MiB) cannot admit a buffered response that is within every per-response ceiling.

public_signal.transport: complete HTTP response replacing backend status; gRPC: HTTP 200 trailers-only grpc-status 8 grpc-message 'Response buffering capacity exceeded'

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge temporarily lacked gateway memory budget to buffer this response; the backend answered but its response was not delivered.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend is unhealthy or returned 503 (despite X-Gateway-Error: backend_error), or that retrying elsewhere helps immediately.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later; gateway operator: review FERRUM_RESPONSE_BUFFER_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES and why responses are buffered.
outcomes.notes: Doc says 'Do not reuse backend_error for a response that never reached a backend' but this gateway-local refusal carries backend_error (status 503>=500, connection_error=false). Body is the only public discriminator. Not retried by the gateway. No Content-Type header on the HTTP/1.1 / HTTP/2 backend-response path: the gateway builds this body with an empty header map (lab-observed over HTTP/1.1 on 0.9.5 and 0.9.7: UP-015; the v0.9.5 audit had recorded application/json). The HTTP/3 writer was not lab-checked.

outcomes.condition: Aggregate buffered-request budget (FERRUM_REQUEST_BUFFER_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES, default 256 MiB) cannot admit another buffered upload. From v0.9.13 native HTTP/3 buffered uploads (including pre-authentication collectors and the H3 bridge drains) take the same budget.

public_signal.transport: complete HTTP response; gRPC trailers-only grpc-status 8 'Request buffering capacity exceeded'

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge temporarily lacked gateway memory budget to buffer this request body; the request was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the request body is too large or that the backend is at fault.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later; gateway operator: review request buffering budget and plugins that force buffering (WAF, validators, retries).
outcomes.notes: X-Gateway-Error is path-dependent: absent when built by build_request_buffer_capacity_response (pre-dispatch builder), but 'backend_error' when the same refusal returns through the backend-dispatch seam (request_buffer_capacity_backend_response). v0.9.13 (#6009): native HTTP/3 buffered drains reserve from FERRUM_REQUEST_BUFFER_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES and answer 503 / gRPC RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (gateway_buffer_capacity, health-neutral). v0.9.14 (#6022): the H1/H2 terminal final-body drain answers gRPC RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (8) instead of UNAVAILABLE (14), a gRPC-Web client on the plain H3 bridge gets RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED instead of UNAVAILABLE, and the H3 dispatch-stage and bridge drain refusals run the reject-path hooks and are logged on_final_request_body. Plain HTTP keeps 503. The mesh backend-seam refusal (request_buffer_capacity_backend_response) is unchanged. v0.9.17 (#6146, #6150): request_buffer_capacity_backend_response (src/proxy/mod.rs:56470) classifies by the trusted request flavor: native gRPC on every dispatcher, Unix-socket and mesh-mTLS included, gets Trailers-Only grpc-status 8 'Request buffering capacity exceeded'; pass-through gRPC-Web gets a framed grpc-status 8 trailer (HTTP 200); plain HTTP keeps the 503 JSON. Status, body and token unchanged.

outcomes.condition: Aggregate request-decode (decompression inspection) budget cannot admit the working set for a governed request.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge temporarily lacked capacity to inspect (decode) this request body; the request was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the request is malformed or the backend is at fault.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later; gateway operator: review request decode budget.
outcomes.notes: Emitted as a plugin-style reject; X-Gateway-Error presence not confirmed per path.

outcomes.condition: Retained reqwest lane (first attempts not selected for direct H1, or retry attempts): DestinationRule connectionPool.tcp.maxConnections reached for the destination; no socket opened. Eligible bodyless HTTP/1.1 first attempts use upstream.connection_limit.pooled on 0.9.11.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to open another connection to this upstream because a gateway-configured connection ceiling is reached; the request was not sent.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend is down or returned 503 (despite backend_error).
outcomes.remediation: Retry later; gateway operator: review maxConnections for this destination.
outcomes.notes: Same condition on direct-H2/H3/gRPC pools surfaces as 502 'Backend unavailable' + connection_failure (upstream.connection_limit.pooled). WebSocket upgrade path uses the same 503 body (src/proxy/mod.rs:16653). No Content-Type header on the HTTP/1.1 / HTTP/2 backend-response path: the gateway builds this body with an empty header map (lab-observed over HTTP/1.1 on 0.9.5 and 0.9.7: UP-018; the v0.9.5 audit had recorded application/json). The HTTP/3 writer was not lab-checked. v0.9.11: eligible direct-H1 dispatch now uses the pooled typed backend_connection_limit classifier; reqwest remains for ineligible bodies and retry attempts. v0.9.11: this distinct refusal remains on retained reqwest/retry lanes; eligible first-attempt HTTP/1.1 uses the direct Hyper pool and the coarse 502 connection_failure outcome upstream.connection_limit.pooled. UP-018 asserts this exact reqwest signal on 0.9.5/7/8/9/10 and the exact coarse direct-H1 signal on 0.9.11; all-profile hosted qualification is recorded in docs/audit/gateway-0.9.11-delta.md. v0.9.19 (#6777): the body is now the shared constant BACKEND_CONNECTION_LIMIT_ERROR_BODY (src/proxy/mod.rs:53336, :48933); bytes and status unchanged. The pooled lanes now answer the same 503 and body (upstream.connection_limit.pooled) but with X-Gateway-Error connection_failure, so the token alone separates the two; UP-018's direct-H1 lane sees the pooled signal.

outcomes.condition: DestinationRule connectionPool.http.http1MaxPendingRequests reached for the backend (upstream overflow) on the reqwest lane.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge shed this request because a gateway-configured in-flight request limit for the upstream is reached; the request was not sent.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend returned 503 or is unhealthy.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later with backoff; gateway operator: review http1MaxPendingRequests.
outcomes.notes: Carries backend_error although no backend was contacted.

outcomes.condition: Literal-IP backend (or dns_override) blocked by the backend egress policy; no dial.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to contact the configured backend address because gateway egress policy blocks it.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend returned an error or is down.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: fix the backend address or egress allow/deny policy.
outcomes.notes: H3 cross-protocol bridge additionally sets gateway-error-reason: backend-egress-policy-denied (src/http3/cross_protocol.rs:2575).

outcomes.condition: reqwest dispatch where proxy dns_override conflicts with a literal-IP backend URL host.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"backend DNS override cannot be applied to literal target"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to dispatch because the route's DNS override cannot be applied to the configured literal backend address (gateway configuration issue).
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend is at fault.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: correct the route's dns_override/backend host.

outcomes.condition: Backend TLS SNI override that neither the direct-H2 pool nor the reqwest dial can honor.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to dispatch because the route's backend TLS server-name override cannot be honored on this path (gateway configuration issue).
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend certificate is wrong or the backend failed.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: review the BackendTLSPolicy/SNI override and backend protocol.
outcomes.notes: gateway-error-reason is an undocumented gateway-authored response header; it is NOT stripped from backend responses, so it is spoofable.

outcomes.condition: Mesh-only: target requires HBONE / sidecar mTLS / Unix-socket transport that is unavailable for this attempt.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Bad Gateway","message":"Mesh transport dispatch required for this backend target"} | {"error":"Bad Gateway","message":"Unix socket retry dispatch unavailable"}
public_signal.transport: complete HTTP response; gRPC trailers-only UNAVAILABLE

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to dispatch because the secured mesh transport required for this backend was unavailable.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend application failed.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway/mesh operator: check gateway mesh identity and transport availability.
outcomes.notes: Mesh deployments only; included for completeness. Reason strings include 'mesh transport dispatch required for this backend target', 'Unix socket retry dispatch is unavailable', 'HBONE transport or gateway identity is unavailable for retry target'.

outcomes.condition: Backend returned a complete 5xx response other than 504 (connection_error=false).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The response was relayed by Ferrum Edge with a 5xx status that, per the gateway's coarse marker, came from or after the upstream exchange; the marker alone does not prove the backend application authored it.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the gateway failed, or (without body/provenance evidence) that the application itself produced it: several gateway-local refusals also carry backend_error.
outcomes.remediation: API owner: inspect backend logs for this request; compare body with known gateway bodies.
outcomes.notes: Backend-supplied X-Gateway-Error values are stripped and replaced on this path (src/proxy/mod.rs:46460). v0.9.8 writes the token on every HTTP/3 path (streaming relays native or bridged, and the bridge's buffered path; #5783) and on the H1/H2 native gRPC builders for a gRPC backend's HTTP 5xx (#5798); on v0.9.7 those relayed a backend 5xx without a token. v0.9.17 (#6127, issue #6109): a backend 508 is never retried, whatever retryable_status_codes lists (src/retry.rs:2006); a downstream Ferrum hop's 508 loop refusal is relayed with backend_error like any backend 5xx.

outcomes.condition: Backend itself returned a complete 504 response (e.g. an upstream load balancer timeout).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: A 504 was relayed through Ferrum Edge and marked backend_timeout; the marker is also applied when the backend itself answered 504, so only the body distinguishes it from the gateway's own timeout.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the gateway timed out (unless the body is exactly {"error":"Backend timeout"} or, on v0.9.6+, {"error":"Request timeout"} from a trusted Ferrum destination).
outcomes.remediation: API owner/infra behind the gateway: check the backend's own upstream timeouts.
outcomes.notes: http_observability_error_class keys backend_timeout on status 504 alone, not on ErrorClass. v0.9.6+: the gateway-authored route-deadline 504 carries {"error":"Request timeout"} (upstream.route_request_timeout.*); a backend can send either literal body. v0.9.19 (#6777): the gateway's own connect-timeout 504 now uses the {"error":"Backend timeout"} body too, but carries connection_failure (connection_error=true, src/retry.rs:302), so a 504 with backend_timeout still means the gateway's read/attempt timeout or the backend's own 504.

outcomes.condition: Backend returned 1xx-4xx (including its own 401/403/404/429).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The upstream application's response was relayed; no gateway failure marker is present.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That a 401/403/404/429 came from the gateway (gateway plugin rejections use the same statuses).
outcomes.remediation: Treat as application result unless other provenance says otherwise.
outcomes.notes: Any X-Gateway-Error or X-Gateway-Upstream-Status the backend sets is stripped at every backend response boundary, in headers or trailers (v0.9.8, #5759; src/proxy/headers.rs:1149).

outcomes.condition: All targets in the upstream (or selected subset) were unhealthy; the load balancer used the all-unhealthy / parent-upstream fallback. Any final status.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge reports it routed this request in degraded mode because no upstream target was considered healthy; the request itself may still have succeeded.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the request failed, or which target was used.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator/API owner: investigate health-check failures for the upstream.
outcomes.notes: v0.9.8 (#5759): a backend- or hook-written X-Gateway-Upstream-Status is stripped on the H1/H2 backend-response builder and on every HTTP/3 response, and the gateway writes 'degraded' once, only when it used fallback routing (v0.9.7 passed a backend copy through on H1/H2 and duplicated it on fallback). Plugin reject paths still keep a plugin-written copy, and any non-Ferrum endpoint can send it: treat as spoofable.

outcomes.condition: Data-plane mode: last applied CP snapshot older than FERRUM_DP_CONFIG_MAX_STALE_SECONDS (default 3600) with CP authority lost and FERRUM_DP_CONFIG_STALE_ACTION=fail_closed (default).

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response. Native gRPC: HTTP 200 trailers-only grpc-status 14 grpc-message 'Gateway configuration stale' WITHOUT X-Gateway-Error. TCP/UDP listeners: accepted socket dropped / datagram session refused (no payload).

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused new work because its data plane has not received a fresh configuration from its control plane within the allowed window; the request was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the client payload, credentials, or the backend are at fault.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: restore control-plane connectivity / config sync; client can retry later (not dispatched).
outcomes.notes: Runs before routing, plugins and overload admission. Already-accepted connections drain. Readiness also degrades (/health ready:false). On the HTTP/3 frontend the native-gRPC variant DOES carry x-gateway-error: config_stale (protocol.grpc.config_stale_h3), and the H3 overload fence runs before this one. WebSocket upgrades get the HTTP 503. FERRUM_DP_CONFIG_STALE_ACTION=readiness_only produces no client signal. v0.9.9 (#5882): ConfigSync accepts only the same build (<crate version>+configsync.r<revision>); a DP of another build is refused with FAILED_PRECONDITION and keeps serving its last-known-good config, so a CP/DP version skew now ends in this 503 once FERRUM_DP_CONFIG_MAX_STALE_SECONDS passes instead of syncing across minor versions.

outcomes.condition: Overload manager critical request pressure (FERRUM_MAX_REQUESTS with FERRUM_OVERLOAD_REQ_CRITICAL_THRESHOLD default 0.95) OR shutdown drain started (SIGTERM).

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response. Native gRPC: HTTP 200 trailers-only grpc-status 14 'Service overloaded' without X-Gateway-Error.

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to admit this request because the gateway process is shedding load or is draining for shutdown; no upstream was contacted for this request.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend is unhealthy, that it is CPU overload specifically, or which of overload vs shutdown drain applied.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later with backoff (safe: request was not dispatched); gateway operator should check overload manager pressure and deployment/shutdown activity.
outcomes.notes: Drain and overload produce byte-identical responses; drain/pressure additionally add 'connection: close' to other responses (mod.rs:41044-41064). FERRUM_MAX_REQUESTS defaults to 0 (request-based shedding off). HTTP/3 native-gRPC variant carries x-gateway-error: overload (protocol.grpc.overload_h3). On HTTP/2 a drain also sends GOAWAY(NO_ERROR) via hyper graceful_shutdown.

outcomes.condition: Critical connection pressure (reject_new_connections) or the listener connection semaphore (FERRUM_MAX_CONNECTIONS, default 100000) exhausted; for TCP listeners also the stale-config fence.

public_signal.transport: accepted TCP socket dropped immediately before TLS/HTTP (code comment says 'TCP RST'; kernel may emit FIN or RST)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The connection to the gateway endpoint was closed before any TLS or HTTP response; this is consistent with gateway connection admission (overload, connection limit, stale config for L4) but also with any network middlebox or a non-listening service.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That Ferrum refused it (no Ferrum marker is possible here), or any HTTP status.
outcomes.remediation: Retry with backoff; compare with a direct health check; gateway operator can check reject/connection-limit counters.
outcomes.notes: No HTTP response possible. H3 equivalent: QUIC Incoming.refuse() (src/http3/server.rs:1802). v0.9.15 (#6085): an HTTP/3 Initial from an unvalidated source runs inside FERRUM_HTTP3_MAX_UNVALIDATED_HANDSHAKES (default 1024) and is charged to the shared connection budget only after its handshake; over that budget the source gets a stateless QUIC Retry, not a refusal (src/http3/server.rs:1814).

outcomes.condition: Circuit breaker for the proxy/target is open (or half-open probe slot taken).

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response. Native gRPC: normalized to trailers-only grpc-status 14 (503->UNAVAILABLE) with grpc-message 'Service temporarily unavailable (circuit breaker open)'; x-gateway-error header is restored into the reject header map so it is expected on gRPC too (not lab-verified).

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected this attempt at its circuit breaker because recent failures to this upstream exceeded the configured threshold; this attempt was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That no earlier retry attempt in the same request reached a backend, or that the backend is still failing now.
outcomes.remediation: Wait for the breaker cooldown and retry; API owner/gateway operator: investigate the upstream's recent failures.
outcomes.notes: Runs through after_proxy reject hooks (headers may be decorated) then the token is restored authoritatively. rejection_phase=circuit_breaker_open in logs.

outcomes.condition: FERRUM_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_PER_IP (default 0 = off) exceeded for the resolved client IP.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Too many concurrent requests from this IP"}
public_signal.transport: HTTP/WebSocket: complete JSON 429; native gRPC: HTTP 200 Trailers-Only grpc-status 8 'Too many concurrent requests from this IP'; gRPC-Web: HTTP 200 framed trailer grpc-status 8

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge limited this request because too many requests from the same client IP were in flight at once.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That an API rate-limit quota (rate_limiting plugin) was exhausted.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: reduce concurrency from this IP; no Retry-After is provided.
outcomes.notes: Pre-routing; no plugins run; no Retry-After / rate-limit headers; gRPC not specially mapped here (plain JSON). v0.9.15 (#6079): the per-IP budget groups native IPv6 clients by FERRUM_PER_IP_IPV6_PREFIX (default /64; 128 restores per-address), so IPv6 clients that share a prefix share one budget; IPv4 and IPv4-mapped IPv6 stay per-address. v0.9.20 (#6965): native gRPC and gRPC-Web are framed on HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 (src/proxy/mod.rs:35855); the earlier note 'gRPC not specially mapped here (plain JSON)' no longer holds. HTTP/3 enforced the same limit with the same framing at v0.9.15 already (src/http3/server.rs:3966 at v0.9.20), so http3 is added to protocols. Still no Retry-After.

outcomes.condition: Connection authenticated with a client certificate whose trust decision was withdrawn by an accepted client-CA/CRL reload (issue #3857).

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response; gRPC: trailers-only grpc-status 16 'Client certificate trust withdrawn'

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge no longer trusts the client certificate this connection was established with; new requests on it are refused.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the API credential/token is wrong.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: reconnect with a currently trusted client certificate; operator: check client CA/CRL changes.
outcomes.notes: v0.9.19 (#6779, issue #6774): the HTTP 401 carries WWW-Authenticate: ClientCertificate realm="ferrum-edge" (src/proxy/mod.rs:56285 build_client_trust_withdrawn_response; constant src/plugins/utils/auth_flow.rs CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_AUTHENTICATION_CHALLENGE). Native gRPC Trailers-Only 16 unchanged. An H1/H2 request whose connection the gateway closes for this reason before any response head is logged 444 (gateway_close_client_trust_withdrawn, gRPC UNAUTHENTICATED; src/proxy/client_abort_scope.rs:123) and the client sees only the close.

outcomes.condition: HTTPS (H1/H2): the request carries Early-Data: 1 (added by a trusted CDN per RFC 8470) and its method is not in the configured early-data method list. HTTP/3: the request stream was accepted while the QUIC handshake was still pending at its own per-stream check (v0.9.8) (0.5-RTT window, listener with FERRUM_TLS_EARLY_DATA_METHODS and no frontend mTLS) and its method is not in that list; checked before routing, so no proxy_id is logged. From v0.9.17 (#6117) HTTP/2 gates an RFC 8441 WebSocket on its wire method CONNECT (not the GET that routing and plugins see), so FERRUM_TLS_EARLY_DATA_METHODS=GET alone refuses Extended CONNECT early data with 425; listing CONNECT also admits HBONE CONNECT early data. The unset default is unchanged.

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response; gRPC: trailers-only grpc-status 14

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to process this request as TLS 0-RTT early data; resend it after the handshake completes.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the method is unsupported by the API.
outcomes.remediation: Caller/CDN: retry without early data.
outcomes.notes: Anvil lab `early` (EARLY-002, EARLY-006) observes both paths with the same public signal. v0.9.8 (#5761): the HTTP/3 accept loop re-checks quinn's handshake-completion signal for every accepted stream, so a 1-RTT request that arrives with the client's Finished is no longer classified as early data (on v0.9.7 it could draw this 425). A 0-RTT request checked after the handshake completed is handled as 1-RTT (RFC 8470 section 6.4); EARLY-001 and EARLY-002 record such a round as a missed window, not as this outcome. v0.9.15 (#6085): the HTTP/3 0.5-RTT path, where this per-stream check can find the handshake pending, is reserved for a source address validated before the handshake began (a Retry or NEW_TOKEN token, src/http3/server.rs:2550); an unvalidated source completes the 1-RTT handshake first, so its 0-RTT request is handled as 1-RTT and never gets this 425. Anvil keeps the server's NEW_TOKEN tokens per session-ticket context so its 0-RTT reconnection is validated. v0.9.17 (#6117): wire-method gate at src/proxy/mod.rs:35749. v0.9.20 (#6965): gRPC-Web now gets a framed grpc-status 14 trailer (src/proxy/mod.rs:35757); native gRPC already got Trailers-Only 14.

outcomes.condition: No proxy route matched the request host/path.

other_headers.x-request-id: only when a GLOBAL correlation_id plugin is configured (configured header_name, honouring inbound_policy and echo_downstream)

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response; gRPC: trailers-only grpc-status 12 grpc-message 'Not Found'

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The endpoint answered 404 with Ferrum's route-miss body shape; if the destination is a trusted Ferrum gateway this means no gateway route matched this host/path.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That every 404 is a gateway route miss (backends can return the same bytes), or that the resource does not exist in the API.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: check host, path prefix and scheme against the published API; gateway operator: check route configuration.
outcomes.notes: Pre-plugin: no auth/CORS plugins run, so a browser CORS failure may mask it. No Via header on this gateway-built response. Mesh: on v0.9.5 and v0.9.7 an inbound HBONE CONNECT whose authority the terminator does not own was also refused with this 404 at relay synthesis (debug log only); v0.9.8 answers it with protocol.hbone.relay_destination_denied (403) or protocol.hbone.relay_not_ready (503) instead (#5763). v0.9.9: config reloads no longer answer this 404 on Gateway API listener routes that were already serving, and a newly bound listener does not accept connections before its route admission is published (#5913, #5914, #5918); a retired listener's connections now get gateway.routing.listener_retired (421) instead of a 404 (#5921, #5927). A wrong-class route on a process-global port no longer blacks out that frontend with this 404 for every route: it is refused at config validation (#5922, #5927). With FERRUM_DIAGNOSTIC_REFS=all the 404 also carries X-Ferrum-Diagnostic-Ref (#5857). v0.9.19 (#6938, issue #6907): global correlation_id policies run on route misses on HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 and add their echo header to this 404 (src/proxy/mod.rs:36429). v0.9.19 (#6709): a HEAD route miss carries no body bytes on HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 (Content-Length kept). v0.9.19 (#6827): every route miss is counted in ferrum_unmatched_requests_total (operator-only; src/diagnostic_ref.rs record_route_miss).

source.symbol: HTTP/2 Extended CONNECT WebSocket evaluated as GET

outcomes.condition: Route matched but the method is not in the route's allowed_methods. From v0.9.15 an HTTP/2 Extended CONNECT or HTTP/3 :protocol=websocket request is evaluated as GET.

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response; gRPC: trailers-only grpc-status 12

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The route exists but does not accept this HTTP method; the Allow header lists the accepted methods.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That authentication failed or the resource is missing.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: use one of the methods in Allow.
outcomes.notes: rejection_phase=allowed_methods (logs only). Allow is gateway-authoritative (policy cannot alter it). v0.9.15 (#6080; issue #6098 / #6099): HTTP/2 Extended CONNECT and HTTP/3 :protocol=websocket requests are evaluated as GET, the method of the backend WebSocket handshake, by allowed_methods (and by mesh_authz :method and opa input.method), as HTTP/1.1 Upgrade already was; a WebSocket route whose allowed_methods lists CONNECT but not GET now answers this 405 to those requests. Plain CONNECT and CONNECT-UDP keep CONNECT, and the 0-RTT method gate still reads the wire method. v0.9.19 (#6709): a HEAD request refused with this 405 gets no body bytes on HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 (Content-Length kept); HTTP/1.1 was already bodiless. Status, body, Allow and gRPC 12 unchanged.

other_headers.Allow: GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete JSON 405 with Allow; TRACE with a native gRPC or gRPC-Web Content-Type: HTTP 200 Trailers-Only / framed grpc-status 12 (UNIMPLEMENTED) grpc-message 'TRACE method is not allowed', Allow kept; CONNECT is never gRPC-framed

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge blocks this HTTP method at the protocol level for all routes.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the route does not exist.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: do not use TRACE/CONNECT through the gateway.
outcomes.notes: v0.9.15 (#6080): a non-GET HTTP/1.1 WebSocket upgrade has its own 405 with Allow: GET (gateway.routing.websocket_upgrade_requires_get). v0.9.20 (#6965): TRACE answers gRPC and gRPC-Web with UNIMPLEMENTED through pre_routing_method_not_allowed_response (src/proxy/mod.rs:34807, call :35675), keeping Allow. v0.9.20 (#6969): a CONNECT that is not a WebSocket Extended CONNECT is always classified plain HTTP on HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, so a refused CONNECT with a gRPC Content-Type keeps the JSON 405 instead of a 200 that clients read as an established tunnel.

outcomes.condition: Request with application/grpc content-type using a method other than POST.

public_signal.transport: trailers-only gRPC response (400 mapped to INVALID_ARGUMENT)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the gRPC call because gRPC requires POST.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the service/method does not exist.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: send gRPC calls with POST.
outcomes.notes: Logged/metric status is 400. v0.9.20 (#6969): a mesh HBONE CONNECT that declares a gRPC or gRPC-Web Content-Type is refused before routing with a PLAIN HTTP 400 {"error":"gRPC requires POST method"} (src/proxy/mod.rs:35720), never Trailers-Only; that is a separate outcome (gateway.routing.hbone_connect_grpc_content_type). This Trailers-Only form (src/proxy/mod.rs:36748) is unchanged.

outcomes.condition: One request header (name+value bytes) exceeds FERRUM_MAX_SINGLE_HEADER_SIZE_BYTES (default 16384).

public_signal.transport: HTTP and gRPC-Web: complete JSON 431 (gRPC-Web keeps JSON because its response media type is negotiated from the very headers being limited); native gRPC: HTTP 200 Trailers-Only grpc-status 8 grpc-message 'Request header exceeds maximum size'

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request because one header is larger than the gateway allows; the body names the header.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend rejected it.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: shrink the named header (often cookies or tokens).
outcomes.notes: Header name echoed (JSON-escaped). H1 parser buffer floor is 8 KiB above which hyper itself may reject first (see frontend_parse.hyper_default_rejects). v0.9.20 (#6965): native gRPC header-limit refusals on HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 are Trailers-Only RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (src/proxy/mod.rs:35382); gRPC-Web keeps the JSON 431, as on HTTP/3 (which already answered native gRPC this way at v0.9.15).

public_signal.transport: HTTP and gRPC-Web: complete JSON 431 (gRPC-Web keeps JSON because its response media type is negotiated from the very headers being limited); native gRPC: HTTP 200 Trailers-Only grpc-status 8 grpc-message 'Total request headers exceed maximum size'

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request because its headers are larger in total than the gateway allows.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend rejected it.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: reduce header size.
outcomes.notes: On HTTP/1 a head larger than the hyper parser buffer (max(limit, 8 KiB)) is rejected by hyper before this check with hyper's own response. v0.9.20 (#6965): native gRPC header-limit refusals on HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 are Trailers-Only RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (src/proxy/mod.rs:35399); gRPC-Web keeps the JSON 431, as on HTTP/3 (which already answered native gRPC this way at v0.9.15).

public_signal.transport: HTTP and gRPC-Web: complete JSON 431 (gRPC-Web keeps JSON because its response media type is negotiated from the very headers being limited); native gRPC: HTTP 200 Trailers-Only grpc-status 8 grpc-message 'Request header count exceeds maximum'

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request because it has more header fields than the gateway allows.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend rejected it.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: send fewer headers.
outcomes.notes: v0.9.20 (#6965): native gRPC header-limit refusals on HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 are Trailers-Only RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (src/proxy/mod.rs:35411); gRPC-Web keeps the JSON 431, as on HTTP/3 (which already answered native gRPC this way at v0.9.15). v0.9.17 (#6127): the hop-limit stamp adds X-Ferrum-Hops after this check (src/proxy/mod.rs:35432), so a request exactly at FERRUM_MAX_HEADER_COUNT can be refused with this 431 at the NEXT Ferrum hop that enforces the same limit (src/proxy/hop_limit.rs module docs).

outcomes.remediation: Caller: send fewer query parameters.

HTTP/3 already did this at v0.9.15, so the catalog's grpc_status null was wrong for HTTP/3 too. Call site src/proxy/mod.rs:35555.

outcomes.condition: Request body exceeds the effective limit (FERRUM_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_SIZE_BYTES default 10485760, FERRUM_MAX_GRPC_RECV_SIZE_BYTES default 4194304 for gRPC, or a lower route/request_size_limiting limit) while buffering or by Content-Length.

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response; gRPC: trailers-only grpc-status 8 'Request body exceeds maximum size of <limit> bytes'

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request because its body exceeds the gateway's size limit.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend received the full body (for streamed uploads the backend may have received a truncated prefix).
outcomes.remediation: Caller: reduce the payload or use a chunked/multipart upload API; operator may review the limit.
outcomes.notes: The request_size_limiting plugin uses a different body shape ({"error":...,"limit":N}); see plugin outcomes. For streamed uploads exceeding the limit mid-stream the backend receives a truncated upload; client-visible shape depends on path (not fully audited). v0.9.14 (#6022): the native-H3 buffered, cross-protocol and native dispatch drains commit this 413 through the shared terminal path (src/http3/server.rs:515), running the reject-path after_proxy and committed-response hooks and logging on_final_request_body, so reject-path decorations can now appear on it. Status, body and gRPC status 8 are unchanged; pre-authentication drains are unchanged. v0.9.19 (#6875): request_size_limiting's 413 now uses this exact body {"error":"Request body exceeds maximum size"} (no "limit" field), and the H3 bridge returns it too, so the body no longer separates the plugin from the core limit; the plugin's limit and reason are only in request metadata. Also v0.9.19 (#6875, #6939): HTTP/2 GET/HEAD/OPTIONS uploads without Content-Length to HTTP/1.1 backends, and unknown-length GET/HEAD uploads to unclassified HTTPS backends, are now forwarded through the size-limited adapter, so over-limit ones reach this 413 instead of being sent as an empty body. Check the plugin outcome id in the D_policy slice.

outcomes.condition: Client upload stalled beyond the request body read timeout while the gateway was buffering it.

outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend timed out.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: check local upload throughput / proxy; operator: review request body timeout.

outcomes.condition: The client proved it went away (its own reset, STOP_SENDING, connection close or I/O error) before the response head: while the gateway buffered or relayed its upload, or (v0.9.19) while any H1/H2 handler phase was still pending.

public_signal.transport: log/metrics vocabulary only: the departed client is never sent this 499; native gRPC accounting records CANCELLED (1)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The client side ended the upload before the gateway received the full request.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the gateway or backend failed.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: check local cancellation/network.
outcomes.notes: 499 is a gateway-internal status recorded in logs/metrics. v0.9.14 (#6022): every streaming upload dispatcher now requires an HTTP/2 client's own END_STREAM; a client RST_STREAM(NO_ERROR) reaches an HTTP/2 backend as RST_STREAM(CANCEL), an HTTP/1.1 backend as an aborted body, and a native HTTP/3 backend as H3_REQUEST_CANCELLED, never as a complete body; the native HTTP/3 request then ends as this 499 client disconnect (src/http3/server.rs:794). Bodies buffered before dispatch are not covered. v0.9.17 (#6146, #6150): early H1/H2 prebuffers, terminal-body drains and buffered H3/gRPC bridges classify client cancellation as client_disconnect, 499 / gRPC CANCELLED, health-neutral; http_reject_status_to_grpc_status maps 499 -> CANCELLED (src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:3150). v0.9.19 (#6780, #6781, #6778): one terminal defined in src/proxy/client_abort.rs:42-53 for every HTTP/3 and gRPC path and for H1/H2 handlers hyper drops (ClientAbortScope, src/proxy/client_abort_scope.rs:81). Only typed client-abort evidence yields 499; a local HTTP/2 protocol reset is logged 400 (protocol_error_before_response), a gateway-closed connection 444 (gateway_close_*), an H3 stream the gateway closed 503 / UNAVAILABLE, and a malformed upload 400 Malformed request body (gateway.client_upload_malformed). Transaction records gain response_delivery (#6769).

outcomes.condition: Request smuggling / desync checks on headers: HTTP/1.0 with Transfer-Encoding, both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding, invalid/non-numeric/overflowing/conflicting Content-Length, H2/H3 with Transfer-Encoding, invalid TE, missing/duplicate/invalid Host on HTTP/1.1. From v0.9.19 (#6882) also: more than one Authorization field line, or one Authorization value carrying a second credential after a top-level comma (all HTTP versions, WebSocket upgrades included), refused before routing and authentication.

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request as malformed or ambiguous at the HTTP protocol layer before routing; the body names the rule.
