outcomes.must_not_claim: That the datagram was delivered, rejected by policy, or that the gateway is down.
outcomes.remediation: Check gateway UDP session/drop counters and backend reachability.
outcomes.notes: Default udp_max_response_amplification_factor 8.0 can silently truncate reply volume. v0.9.15 (#6079): FERRUM_UDP_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_IP groups native IPv6 sources by FERRUM_PER_IP_IPV6_PREFIX (default /64), and udp_rate_limiting IP keys use a fixed /64. DTLS passthrough drops a ClientHello whose SNI is malformed or unrepresentable before catch-all routing (#6080, src/proxy/udp_proxy.rs:2240); a well-formed ClientHello without SNI can still use the catch-all. v0.9.19 (#6868, issue #6868): sessions carry a UdpDatagramPolicyFence (src/proxy/udp_proxy.rs:675, check at :691); a plain-UDP worker that sees a changed datagram-hook digest drops the queued datagram and retires the session (src/proxy/udp_proxy.rs:1303), the client's next datagram opens a new session with a new backend source port. DTLS sessions end the same way (src/proxy/udp_proxy.rs:8119) and the client gets the usual relay-end close (it must handshake again). Reloads that leave the datagram-hook configs unchanged do not end sessions. udp_rate_limiting gains ipv6_prefix and direction (plugin outcome, slice D).

outcomes.condition: Frontend DTLS client certificate invalid / refused, or backend DTLS origination failure (including, since v0.9.17 #6119, a backend whose TLS material this node refused: src/dtls/mod.rs:1139).

public_signal.transport: frontend DTLS client-cert refusal (FERRUM_DTLS_CLIENT_CA_CERT_PATH): server discards its queued final flight (src/dtls/mod.rs:4250-4261); code comment (src/dtls/mod.rs:4269-4270) says dimpl close() during an in-progress handshake queues no alert, so a DTLS 1.2 client sees an incomplete handshake/retransmits; DTLS 1.3 peer is torn down after the server Finished

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The DTLS handshake with the gateway was refused or did not complete.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend rejected application data.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: check DTLS client certificate/trust.
outcomes.notes: Code comment and docs/frontend_tls.md:217-239 disagree on whether an alert is sent under DTLS 1.2 (doc: 'emits the refusal alert'; code comment: close() queues no alert during an in-progress handshake). Lab-verify. Backend DTLS origination failures are only visible as silence (StreamSetupKind::BackendDtlsHandshake). v0.9.20 (#7001, issue #7000): the vendored dimpl 0.6.1 DTLS 1.3 CertificateRequest no longer carries an empty certificate_authorities extension (vendor/dimpl-0.6.1-ferrum-patched/src/dtls13/server.rs:1405, only signature_algorithms at :1414; docs/frontend_tls.md:223-227). Through v0.9.19 a strict DTLS 1.3 client (dimpl >= 0.8, Chrome/BoringSSL) dropped that CertificateRequest without an alert and its handshake timed out even with a valid certificate, so on v0.9.15-v0.9.19 a DTLS 1.3 handshake timeout against a client-cert listener does not by itself show a certificate refusal; on v0.9.20 such a client completes and only a real refusal fails. Refusal behaviour (discard, no alert under DTLS 1.2 per the code comment, refused session never relayed) is unchanged; docs/frontend_tls.md:231 still says the refusal alert is emitted, so the doc/code disagreement stands.

outcomes.condition: A build-time custom plugin (custom_plugins/*.rs, FERRUM_CUSTOM_PLUGINS) returns PluginResult::Reject/RejectBinary from any hook, with any status, body and headers.

other_headers.Content-Type: application/json unless the plugin sets one

public_signal.transport: complete HTTP response; gRPC trailers-only; WS pre-upgrade HTTP; L4 close
public_signal.x_gateway_error_note: whatever the plugin sets (not sanitized on reject paths)
public_signal.http_status_note: plugin-chosen (a status outside 100-999 falls back by phase: 500 on_request_received / 401 authenticate / 403 authorize / 500 body and before_proxy phases)
public_signal.grpc_status_note: mapped from HTTP status unless the plugin sets grpc-status

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: A gateway-side plugin (possibly a custom one) returned this response; without the plugin's own documentation its meaning cannot be derived from the source audit.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Any specific built-in cause, or that the backend produced it, or that an X-Gateway-Error value on this response is gateway-core authored.
outcomes.remediation: Ask the gateway operator for the custom plugin's contract; add a signed/schema-validated local rule extension if needed.
outcomes.notes: PluginFailurePolicy (FailClosed / KeepLastKnownGood / OptionalFailOpen, src/plugins/mod.rs:1343-1351) governs only construction/reload failures, not runtime rejects; there is no runtime 'plugin error' status. Hooks return PluginResult, not Result, so there is no request-time plugin-error channel and no per-hook HTTP timeout (gRPC calls end at the client deadline with grpc-status 4 'Deadline exceeded at gateway'). Release builds use panic = "abort" (Cargo.toml:507), so a panic in any plugin kills the whole gateway process and resets every in-flight connection; there is no generic 500. A custom plugin that produces response bodies without declaring response_body_production surfaces as 503 {"error":"Response buffering capacity exceeded"}. See also plugin.custom.* records. v0.9.19 (#6641, issue #6614): equal-priority instances now run in a deterministic order (priority, plugin name, then scope global/proxy/proxy-group, then plugin-config id; src/plugin_cache.rs:5187), so which of two equal-priority plugins rejects first no longer depends on config/DB order. v0.9.20 (#6975): built-ins skip undeclared lifecycle hooks; custom plugins still default to every hook (unchanged).

outcomes.condition: adaptive_concurrency plugin (backend-admission phase) has no permit for the target (TargetLimit) or is handing off between policy generations.

public_signal.transport: complete HTTP response; native gRPC trailers-only 200 grpc-status 14 with x-gateway-error kept

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge shed this request at its adaptive concurrency limit for the upstream; the request was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the API applied a rate limit, or that the backend crashed (the limit adapts to observed backend latency/errors, so the backend may be slow).
outcomes.remediation: Retry with backoff (no Retry-After is sent); gateway operator/API owner: check upstream latency and adaptive_concurrency settings.
outcomes.notes: Only source of the concurrency_limit token. Not authoritatively restored after reject hooks (unlike circuit_breaker_open). Other 503 shedders use no token: 'Destination active request limit reached', 'WebSocket connection limit exceeded'. v0.9.8 (#5737): the latency baseline is the minimum of the current and previous window of baseline_window_samples (default 1000) healthy samples, so one unusually fast response no longer tightens the limit forever; fewer spurious 503s under steady load. v0.9.20 (#7004): streaming-eligible ai_federation provider destinations, and every route-override plugin's trigger, are now part of the route key, so a reload that moves such a destination resets the learned limits instead of admitting the new destination as an untracked bypass. v0.9.19 (#6879, #6941): decision metrics and upload-neutral H2 timing (operator-only). The 503 / concurrency_limit signal is unchanged (src/plugins/adaptive_concurrency.rs:150).

outcomes.condition: The request arrived with an X-Ferrum-Hops value at or above FERRUM_MAX_PROXY_HOPS (default 10, max 255; 0 disables the feature). Every Ferrum gateway increments and forwards this gateway-owned request header on every HTTP-family hop (backend dispatch, retries, WebSocket, HBONE/mesh replay, request-scoped plugin calls), so the usual cause is a routing loop: a route whose upstream resolves back to a Ferrum gateway (self-referencing target, DNS change) or a cycle across gateways. A client can also send a high value. Checked once per request before routing and before any plugin, after the header size/count limits.

public_signal.transport: HTTP, WebSocket upgrade and gRPC-Web: complete JSON 508 with X-Gateway-Error: loop_detected; native gRPC: HTTP 200 Trailers-Only grpc-status 9 (FAILED_PRECONDITION) grpc-message 'Proxy hop limit exceeded' with no token

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: A Ferrum Edge gateway refused this request with 508 Loop Detected before routing because the X-Ferrum-Hops count it received had reached its proxy hop limit; the refusing gateway contacted no backend. Every Ferrum hop increments the count, so a routing loop or a long gateway chain is the usual cause, but the header can also come from the caller or an intermediary.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend failed or returned 508, that the gateway is overloaded, how many gateways the request passed through, that a routing loop exists, or which route or hop forms a loop. When an outer Ferrum hop relays this 508 the header reads backend_error, not loop_detected.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: look for a route whose upstream resolves back to a Ferrum gateway (self-referencing target, DNS, mesh egress) and break the cycle; raise FERRUM_MAX_PROXY_HOPS only for a legitimately deep chain. Caller: do not send X-Ferrum-Hops yourself, and check that no proxy in front of the gateway adds or forwards it.
outcomes.notes: New in v0.9.17 (#6127, issue #6109; first tagged in the unpublished v0.9.16). Only the refusing hop writes loop_detected; an outer Ferrum hop relaying the 508 labels it backend_error (src/retry.rs:229 doc) and never retries a backend 508 whatever retryable_status_codes lists (src/retry.rs:2006). gRPC-Web on HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 gets the plain JSON 508 (src/proxy/mod.rs:34851; src/http3/server.rs:20778). No transaction summary is emitted for this fence, so no metric row carries the token; a diagnostic reference records rejection.phase proxy_hop_limit with a null detail.rejection_phase. Stream proxies (tcp, tcp_tls, udp, dtls) are not covered. A mesh inbound route to the local workload checks but does not increment the count (src/proxy/hop_limit.rs:420). Request-scoped plugin calls carry the count from v0.9.17 (#6132), so a plugin target that loops back is refused the same way. Distinguishability: unique status, body and token.

outcomes.condition: NodeWaypoint topology: an HTTP request on a captured connection whose source pod (eBPF cookie identity) is no longer vouched by the live mesh slice — pod withdrawn, its records now conflict, or SPIFFE hash mismatch — checked on every request, not only at accept.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"node-waypoint source identity is no longer enrolled"}
public_signal.transport: complete HTTP response (plain JSON via build_response; no gRPC trailers mapping on this path)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The NodeWaypoint refused the request because the calling pod is no longer enrolled in the mesh slice it serves.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That an AuthorizationPolicy denied the request; that the destination or backend refused it.
outcomes.remediation: Mesh operator: check the source pod's enrollment and the NodeWaypoint slice (counted in /overload node_waypoint_drops; warn 'Refusing node-waypoint request: the source pod identity is no longer vouched'); a reconnect after re-enrollment is admitted.
outcomes.notes: New in v0.9.20 (PR #6964, issue #6800). Before, a withdrawn pod mid-connection was served with no per-pod scope (mesh-wide policy only, or plugin.mesh_authz.per_pod_scope_missing). gRPC clients get the plain HTTP 403 JSON (unverified whether a later layer rewrites it; build_response sets only Content-Type). Unique body.

outcomes.condition: Any gateway-synthesized native gRPC error (H1/H2/H3 frontends): contract shape shared by every gateway gRPC error below.

public_signal.transport: trailers-only: single HEADERS with END_STREAM, no DATA, no Content-Length; h2 may then send its permitted NO_ERROR request reset after the complete response (grpc_proxy.rs:4403-4414) [grpc-message: raw text, CR/LF replaced by space, NOT percent-encoded; omitted when empty]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: A gRPC error returned as HTTP 200 with grpc-status in a single END_STREAM HEADERS block (Trailers-Only) is a terminal RPC failure, whoever authored it.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That HTTP 200 means success, or that a trailing NO_ERROR reset after the END_STREAM HEADERS makes the RPC incomplete.
outcomes.remediation: Read grpc-status/grpc-message as the RPC outcome.
outcomes.notes: Initial-response header policy plugins may add headers. Pre-routing errors use build_grpc_error_response (no policy). Clients must read the END_STREAM HEADERS as terminal even if a NO_ERROR reset follows. v0.9.20 (#6969): a CONNECT is never classified as gRPC (src/proxy/backend_dispatch.rs:66), so a refused plain CONNECT carrying a gRPC Content-Type keeps its HTTP status and JSON body on HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 instead of a trailers-only 200. Builders unchanged (src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:5223, :5247).

outcomes.condition: Any plugin/auth/admission HTTP reject (PluginResult::Reject) on a native gRPC request (H1/H2).

public_signal.transport: trailers-only 200 [grpc-message: reject header grpc-message if present; else first non-empty JSON body key grpc_message|message|error|details; else raw body text; else a reason such as 'Unauthenticated','Permission denied','Resource exhausted','Service unavailable','Unimplemented','Internal error']

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: A gateway plugin rejection on a gRPC call is rendered as Trailers-Only with a grpc-status mapped from the plugin's HTTP status and a grpc-message taken from its body; the grpc-status alone does not identify the plugin.
outcomes.must_not_claim: The original HTTP status or plugin identity from grpc-status alone (e.g. 16 can be any auth plugin, 14 any 502/503).
outcomes.remediation: Inspect grpc-message and any extra headers kept in the HEADERS block (www-authenticate, x-ratelimit-*).
outcomes.notes: grpc-status = plugin-supplied numeric grpc-status header, else mapped from HTTP status. Other plugin reject headers (x-ratelimit-*, www-authenticate, x-gateway-error) are kept in the HEADERS block. serverless_function terminate with authorizing provenance may emit HEADERS+DATA+trailers. v0.9.17 (#6146, #6150): an operator-defined 499 reject (request_termination, fault_injection) without an explicit grpc-status now maps to CANCELLED (1), default message 'Cancelled' (src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:3150, src/proxy/mod.rs:28886); before it fell through to INTERNAL. v0.9.20 (#6969): rejects of a CONNECT are never gRPC-shaped.

outcomes.condition: Stale-config fence on the HTTP/3 frontend for a native gRPC request.

public_signal.transport: H3 trailers-only HEADERS(200)+FIN, then STOP_SENDING(H3_NO_ERROR) [grpc-message: Gateway configuration stale]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused this gRPC call because its data plane configuration is stale; the call was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Any client or backend fault.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: restore control-plane config sync.
outcomes.notes: X-Gateway-Error survives on H3 gRPC but NOT on H1/H2 gRPC (see gateway.admission.config_stale). On H3 the overload fence runs before the stale fence; on H1/H2 stale runs first.

outcomes.condition: Overload/drain on the HTTP/3 frontend for a native gRPC request.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused this gRPC call because the gateway is shedding load or draining; the call was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure; overload vs drain.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later with backoff.
outcomes.notes: H1/H2 gRPC sibling carries no X-Gateway-Error.

outcomes.condition: Route allowed_methods excludes the gRPC request method.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gRPC route exists but its allowed methods exclude this HTTP method.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the RPC method is unimplemented by the service.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: use POST for gRPC; operator: check allowed_methods.
outcomes.notes: Metrics/logs record 405; wire carries 200.

outcomes.condition: Circuit breaker open for a native gRPC request.

public_signal.transport: trailers-only 200 [grpc-message: Service temporarily unavailable (circuit breaker open)]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected this gRPC attempt at its circuit breaker; this attempt was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That no earlier attempt reached a backend, or that the backend is still failing.
outcomes.remediation: Wait for breaker cooldown; investigate upstream failures.
outcomes.notes: X-Gateway-Error restored authoritatively after hooks (mod.rs:34177).

outcomes.condition: adaptive_concurrency shed on a native gRPC request.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge shed this gRPC call at its adaptive concurrency limit for the upstream; it was not sent.
outcomes.must_not_claim: An application rate limit or backend crash.
outcomes.remediation: Retry with backoff; operator: review adaptive_concurrency.
outcomes.notes: No authoritative restore for this token; an after_proxy reject hook could strip it.

outcomes.condition: DestinationRule http2MaxRequests active-request cap reached for the destination.

public_signal.transport: HTTP 503; native gRPC: trailers-only 200 grpc-status 14 [grpc-message: Destination active request limit reached]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused the request because a gateway-configured active-request cap for the destination is reached; it was not sent.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Retry with backoff; operator: review DestinationRule http2MaxRequests.
outcomes.notes: No X-Gateway-Error set by this code.

outcomes.condition: Native gRPC (H1/H2 frontend): GrpcProxyError::BackendUnavailable before response headers (DNS, TCP connect, TLS/h2c handshake, maxConnections refusal, send_request failure/reset), observed before the client RPC deadline. Since v0.9.19 GrpcProxyError::Internal is INTERNAL (protocol.grpc.dispatch_internal_error); since v0.9.20 a failure observed at or after the client deadline is DEADLINE_EXCEEDED (protocol.grpc.client_deadline_exceeded).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway reports it could not obtain a usable response from the gRPC upstream before response headers (connect, DNS, TLS, connection limit, or a failed/reset send); the request may or may not have reached the backend.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Which step failed, whether the backend processed the call, or that the backend itself returned UNAVAILABLE (no X-Gateway-Error on this path).
outcomes.remediation: Retry only idempotent RPCs; gateway operator: check gateway logs error_class for this call.
outcomes.notes: Deliberately generic; X-Gateway-Error is never added on this gRPC path, so gRPC clients get no connection_failure vs backend_error distinction. H3 frontend uses 'Service unavailable' (protocol.grpc.h3_backend_error_mapping). v0.9.8 (#5747): the gRPC-Web form of this terminal (H1/H2 native gRPC path and the HTTP/3 bridge) now runs the reject-path after_proxy decorators, so a browser client gets the CORS headers it needs to read the status; the wording is unchanged. v0.9.19 (#6777): GrpcProxyError::Internal (backend TLS config build failure, invalid backend URL/authority) now answers grpc-status 13 'Internal gateway error' instead of 14 'Backend unavailable' (src/proxy/mod.rs:43444, :43454). v0.9.20 (#6973, #6979): a backend failure observed at or after the client deadline is settled as that deadline, health-neutral (src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:7084 client_deadline_owns_failure).

outcomes.condition: Native gRPC: backend connect/read timeout (backend_*_timeout_ms) before response headers; since v0.9.6 also (H1/H2 frontends, native gRPC and generic-path gRPC/gRPC-Web; v0.9.8 also the HTTP/3 bridge, including gRPC-Web pass-through) the matched route rule's per-attempt budget (Gateway API timeouts.backendRequest / mesh_route_dispatch attempt_timeout_ms) expiring after the request was sent, while waiting for response headers or collecting a buffered response body.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway reports the gRPC upstream did not respond within a gateway-enforced backend bound (backend connect/read timeout, or a route rule's per-attempt timeout).
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the client deadline expired, or which bound (connect, read, or route attempt budget) fired.
outcomes.remediation: API owner: check backend latency; operator: backend timeouts.
outcomes.notes: Distinguish from client deadline ('Deadline exceeded at gateway'). Connect timeout, read timeout and (v0.9.7) a route per-attempt budget share this message. gRPC-Web receives the same status/message in a translated trailer frame. v0.9.8: after_proxy plugins (e.g. CORS) no longer turn this terminal into 'Deadline exceeded at gateway' (#5744), and a gRPC-Web client's terminal now carries the reject-path after_proxy decorations such as CORS headers (#5747). The HTTP/3 bridge tells the backend its remaining budget in grpc-timeout (#5734). v0.9.11: Unauthenticated streamed native gRPC upload write bounds move from the pump into Hyper; a ready chunk blocked on backend capacity expires as the existing grpc-status 4/read_write_timeout before headers, and as a stream reset after headers. Authenticated uploads retain their lifetime pump. v0.9.19 (#6777): sidecar mesh-mTLS native gRPC connect timeouts answer grpc-status 4 'Backend deadline exceeded' instead of 14 'sidecar mTLS backend unavailable' (src/proxy/mod.rs:57424-57427); native HTTP/3 backend connect timeouts likewise (see protocol.grpc.h3_backend_error_mapping). v0.9.20 (#6976, #6979): a buffered native gRPC failure observed after an earlier operator read bound settles as that bound's BackendTimeout.

outcomes.condition: The gateway's RPC deadline expires before a stream was acquired, during buffered upload, or while a buffered response/rejection is still uncommitted (replaces it). The deadline is the client grpc-timeout (as capped/defaulted by a grpc_deadline policy) and, since v0.9.6 (released v0.9.7), a matched Gateway API HTTPRoute rule timeouts.request / mesh_route_dispatch request_timeout_ms folded in (earlier wins); a rule's timeouts.backendRequest / attempt_timeout_ms also ends here when it expires before the request was sent to the backend (v0.9.7 also for any HTTP/3 expiry; v0.9.8 charges an expiry after send on the HTTP/3 bridge as protocol.grpc.backend_timeout, #5734).

public_signal.transport: trailers-only 200; any buffered backend response is discarded [grpc-message: Deadline exceeded at gateway]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gRPC deadline in force at the gateway (the caller's grpc-timeout, possibly capped by gateway policy, or a route-configured request/attempt timeout) expired before a response was delivered.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend slowness as proven cause, or that the caller's own grpc-timeout was the deadline that fired (a route rule timeout produces the identical signal).
outcomes.remediation: Caller: raise grpc-timeout if one was sent or reduce work; operator/API owner: check route rule timeouts (HTTPRoute timeouts.request/backendRequest, mesh_route_dispatch request_timeout_ms/attempt_timeout_ms).
outcomes.notes: Overrides an already-selected plugin/backend error. v0.9.7 and later: route rule timeouts fold into the RPC deadline for gRPC and gRPC-Web on H1/H2/H3 (plugins/mod.rs:4410); the remaining budget is sent upstream as grpc-timeout, so a deadline-aware backend may instead return its own DEADLINE_EXCEEDED (protocol.grpc.backend_status_passthrough). No Ferrum marker distinguishes a route timeout from a client grpc-timeout on the wire. v0.9.11: An earlier captured client deadline remains DEADLINE_EXCEEDED even when authorization expiry is observed later; pre-handoff acquisition/handoff refusals carry distinct internal messages and do not charge backend health. v0.9.13 (#6008): a previewed route total also bounds early (pre-before_proxy) gRPC body collection and ends as DEADLINE_EXCEEDED. v0.9.14 (#6022): pre-handoff and post-send deadline classification uses a typed GrpcDeadlinePhase (src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:2867); client-visible statuses and messages are unchanged. v0.9.20 (#6973, issue #6022; #6979, issue #6976): any backend failure (reset, CANCEL, connect or read error) observed at or after the client RPC deadline is answered as this outcome ('Deadline exceeded at gateway') and is health-neutral, on the native gRPC header waits and body collection, the direct H1/H2 and reqwest header waits, the native HTTP/3 relay and every buffered collect (src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:7084). It is a clock cutoff, not proof of cause; a backend failure observed before the deadline keeps its own outcome.

outcomes.condition: The gateway's RPC deadline (client grpc-timeout / grpc_deadline policy, or since v0.9.6 a folded route timeouts.request or the committed attempt's timeouts.backendRequest budget) fires after response HEADERS were sent but before any response DATA.

public_signal.transport: backend HEADERS then synthesized TRAILERS frame with END_STREAM (percent-encoded message) [grpc-message: Deadline%20exceeded%20at%20gateway]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gRPC deadline in force at the gateway expired after the backend answered with headers but before any message was delivered.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend error, or that the caller's own grpc-timeout (rather than a route-configured timeout) was the deadline that fired.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: review deadline; operator: review route rule timeouts.
outcomes.notes: Backend body dropped. gRPC-Web gets an encoded trailer DATA frame. H3 relay: trailers if 0 DATA offered else RESET_STREAM(H3_INTERNAL_ERROR) (src/http3/server.rs:16983). v0.9.7: a route rule timeout folded into the RPC deadline produces the same terminal. v0.9.19 (#6870): on HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 a gateway-owned response pump enforces the deadline even when the client withholds flow-control credit (src/proxy/body.rs:1378, src/proxy/response_watchdog.rs:731); a client that has not drained the DEADLINE_EXCEEDED terminal within 2 s has its connection closed (TRANSPORT_CLOSE_GRACE, src/proxy/response_watchdog.rs:193), ending sibling streams. An open upload is reset to the backend with RST_STREAM(CANCEL). v0.9.20 (#6982): an already-complete response skips the pump but keeps the expiry and close grace (src/proxy/response_watchdog.rs:440). Trailer shape unchanged.

outcomes.condition: The gateway's RPC deadline (client grpc-timeout / grpc_deadline policy, or since v0.9.6 a folded route timeouts.request or the committed attempt's timeouts.backendRequest budget) fires after response DATA was already sent.

public_signal.transport: stream reset, no trailers (H2 RST_STREAM code chosen by hyper, INTERNAL_ERROR inferred; H3 H3_INTERNAL_ERROR)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The RPC stream was reset after messages were delivered; no terminal gRPC status was received.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Success, a specific grpc-status, or which party caused the reset.
outcomes.remediation: Treat the RPC as incomplete.
outcomes.notes: No terminal status is fabricated once DATA was sent. v0.9.7: route rule timeouts folded into the RPC deadline end the stream the same way. v0.9.19 (#6870): on HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 the deadline is enforced by a gateway timer even when the client withholds credit; the client connection is closed 2 s after the deadline if the terminal was not drained (src/proxy/response_watchdog.rs:193, :731), which can end sibling HTTP/2 streams.

outcomes.condition: Buffered backend gRPC response exceeds the max response body size.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused a buffered gRPC response larger than its response size limit.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend crash.
outcomes.remediation: Reduce response size or raise the limit.
outcomes.notes: H3 frontend message: 'Response payload exceeded limit' (cross_protocol.rs:9126).

outcomes.condition: Client gRPC request body exceeds FERRUM_MAX_GRPC_RECV_SIZE_BYTES (default 4194304) or route limit, detected before response headers.

public_signal.transport: trailers-only 200 [grpc-message: gRPC request payload size exceeds maximum of {N} bytes]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused the gRPC request because its payload exceeds the gateway's gRPC receive limit.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend rejection.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: send smaller messages.
outcomes.notes: Streaming overflow path forwards 'gRPC request payload size exceeds maximum' (mod.rs:35113). Overflow after response headers not traced.

outcomes.condition: Native gRPC: credential expiry or authenticated-stream max lifetime reached before the response head is committed.

public_signal.transport: trailers-only 200 [grpc-message: credential expired | authenticated stream lifetime reached]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway ended the gRPC call because the caller's credential (or maximum authenticated lifetime) expired while the call was in progress.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the credential was invalid at submission.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: refresh credentials.
outcomes.notes: Non-gRPC gets 401 {"error":"Unauthorized"} (auth.authorization_lifetime_expired_before_commit). v0.9.11: The receipt-anchored authorization plan now bounds sender acquisition, final handoff and response-header waits across direct H1/H2, Unix/HBONE, sidecar mesh, native gRPC and H3/bridge dispatch. The earliest captured authorization/client/operator bound retains attribution even on late wakeups; retries cannot extend it. Expiry is latched once, never retried and backend-health neutral. The terminal is unchanged (plain HTTP 401, native gRPC HTTP 200/status 16). A public terminal does not prove whether any request bytes reached the backend. v0.9.13: a buffered native gRPC or gRPC-Web response whose credential expires during the response hooks writes exactly one transaction summary carrying grpc-status 16, and the backend outcome is recorded before the hooks; the expiry terminal keeps only gateway headers whose provenance the completed hooks recorded, so a native gRPC expiry response may omit gateway headers such as correlation IDs. v0.9.14 (#6022): a refused streamed-gRPC handoff keeps the client upload before the Trailers-Only terminal. Status and body unchanged.

outcomes.condition: Native gRPC: credential/lifetime expiry after HEADERS but before DATA.

public_signal.transport: synthesized TRAILERS grpc-status 16 [grpc-message: credential expired | authenticated stream lifetime reached]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway ended the gRPC stream with UNAUTHENTICATED because the caller's credential or maximum authenticated lifetime expired.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend authorization failure.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: refresh credentials and reconnect.
outcomes.notes: Plain HTTP/SSE never gets trailers (see streaming.authorization_lifetime_expired_after_commit). v0.9.11: Source EOF is distinct from transport upload completion. An H2 CANCEL/NO_ERROR cannot become clean EOF, queued bridge DATA checks the original lifetime, and affinity persists through response plus every backend stream. Native H3 resets unfinished uploads with H3_REQUEST_CANCELLED on expiry/error/cancellation. Existing terminals remain; this is no new cause or timing inference.

outcomes.condition: Native gRPC: backend stream error/reset or per-frame idle read timeout after response HEADERS were forwarded.

public_signal.transport: frontend RST_STREAM (hyper chooses the reason: inner h2 Reason if present, else INTERNAL_ERROR); no grpc-status trailers synthesized

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The RPC stream was reset after response headers; no terminal gRPC status was received, so the outcome is unknown.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Success, a specific grpc-status, or that the gateway authored the failure.
outcomes.remediation: Treat as incomplete; retry only idempotent RPCs.
outcomes.notes: A gRPC client typically reports INTERNAL or CANCELLED from its own library mapping; the missing trailer is the evidence. v0.9.11: Source EOF is distinct from transport upload completion. An H2 CANCEL/NO_ERROR cannot become clean EOF, queued bridge DATA checks the original lifetime, and affinity persists through response plus every backend stream. Native H3 resets unfinished uploads with H3_REQUEST_CANCELLED on expiry/error/cancellation. Existing terminals remain; this is no new cause or timing inference. v0.9.14 (#6019): a backend RST_STREAM or GOAWAY with any reason except NO_ERROR that ends a direct-H2 or gRPC response body is body_error_class protocol_error (was request_error, banked as a backend success) and can now open circuit breakers and fail passive health. NO_ERROR still ends the body as an early response. The client-visible cut is unchanged.

outcomes.condition: Backend returns its own gRPC outcome (any grpc-status).

public_signal.transport: backend HTTP status, grpc-status, grpc-message, grpc-status-details-bin forwarded; only hop-by-hop trailer names stripped

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: A grpc-status other than those synthesized by the gateway, delivered with backend headers, is the backend's RPC outcome relayed unchanged.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the gateway authored it.
outcomes.remediation: API owner: inspect service logs.
outcomes.notes: If the backend omits grpc-status, UNKNOWN(2) is recorded in log metadata only; nothing is synthesized. Native gRPC response path adds neither X-Gateway-Error nor alt-svc.

outcomes.condition: Gateway failed to build the gRPC client response.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway failed internally while building the gRPC response.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: logs.
outcomes.notes: Reject-builder fallback at mod.rs:26574 uses 13 with the same message. v0.9.8 (#5758): a pass-through gRPC-Web body (route without the grpc_web plugin) is relayed byte for byte with the backend's own trailer frame; the gateway no longer appends a synthesized grpc-status: 2 frame on HTTP/1.1 / HTTP/2. v0.9.19 (#6777): the grpc-message 'Internal gateway error' is now also sent with grpc-status 13 by protocol.grpc.dispatch_internal_error; this build-failure path still uses 14 (src/proxy/mod.rs:42467-42469), so the status distinguishes them.

outcomes.condition: Mesh only: target needs a mesh transport or Unix socket the direct gRPC pool cannot dial.

public_signal.transport: trailers-only 200 [grpc-message: fixed mesh refusal messages (e.g. 'gRPC to a unix-socket backend cannot be dialed directly', 'HBONE dispatch required for this backend target: {reason}')]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused to dispatch this gRPC call because the required mesh transport is unavailable.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Mesh operator: transport/identity.
outcomes.notes: Mesh deployments only.

outcomes.condition: Native gRPC backend literal IP denied by the backend egress policy.

public_signal.transport: trailers-only 200 [grpc-message: backend address blocked by egress policy]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused to contact the configured gRPC backend address because gateway egress policy blocks it.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Operator: egress policy.

outcomes.condition: Native gRPC: a protected response representation could not be inspected.

public_signal.transport: trailers-only 200 [grpc-message: response representation could not be inspected]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway withheld the gRPC response because a gateway response policy could not inspect it.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend returned INTERNAL.
outcomes.remediation: Operator: response policy / encoding.

outcomes.condition: A gRPC-Web request refused by the request-header size or count limits (single header, total, count): the 431 JSON answer is kept, not framed as gRPC-Web. Before v0.9.19 (H1/H2) this outcome also covered native gRPC header-limit 431s, the per-IP concurrency 429 and protocol-header 400s; those are now gRPC-framed (recorded by A_core on each owning outcome: size.request_header_single_too_large, size.request_headers_total_too_large, size.request_header_count_exceeded, size.url_too_long, size.query_param_count_exceeded, frontend_parse.protocol_header_violation, frontend_parse.host_authority_violation, gateway.admission.per_ip_concurrency, gateway.routing.trace_or_connect_blocked).

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Request header '<name>' exceeds maximum size of <N> bytes"} | {"error":"Total request headers exceed maximum size"} | {"error":"Request header count (<n>) exceeds maximum of <N>"}
public_signal.transport: plain HTTP 431 even for gRPC-Web clients (no trailer frame)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway rejected the gRPC-Web call at the HTTP layer for oversized or too many request headers, so the client saw a JSON 431 instead of a gRPC-Web status.
outcomes.must_not_claim: The grpc-status the client library synthesized from the HTTP status.
outcomes.remediation: Inspect the HTTP status/body; fix headers or concurrency.
outcomes.notes: gRPC clients will apply their own HTTP-to-status mapping (typically UNAVAILABLE/INTERNAL/UNKNOWN), which hides the real cause. v0.9.19 (#6940): native gRPC protocol-header refusals became trailers-only INVALID_ARGUMENT on H1/H2. v0.9.20 (#6965): native gRPC header limits are trailers-only RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (src/proxy/mod.rs:35391, :35405, :35421) and the per-IP 429 is framed for native gRPC and gRPC-Web (src/proxy/mod.rs:35861); only gRPC-Web header-limit refusals stay JSON 431, as on HTTP/3 (src/http3/server.rs:3261 passes no gRPC-Web content type).

outcomes.condition: gRPC over the HTTP/3 frontend: backend dispatch fails before response headers.

public_signal.transport: H3 trailers-only HEADERS(200)+FIN [grpc-message: BackendUnavailable=>14 'Service unavailable'; BackendTimeout and (v0.9.19, native H3 backend) connect timeout=>4 'Backend deadline exceeded'; ClientDeadlineExceeded=>4 'Deadline exceeded at gateway'; ResourceExhausted=>8 'Request payload exceeded backend limit'; ResponseTooLarge=>8 'Response payload exceeded limit'; ResponseBufferCapacity=>8 'Response buffering capacity exceeded'; Internal (incl. v0.9.19 native H3 backend TLS config)=>13 'Internal gateway error'; malformed client trailers=>3 'Malformed request trailers'; malformed client body=>3 'Malformed request body'; upload the gateway closed=>14 'Request stream closed by the gateway'; client upload abort=>1 'Client disconnected' (usually unseen)]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Over HTTP/3 the gateway reports a gRPC upstream failure before response headers with the listed status/message; the backend may or may not have received the call.
outcomes.must_not_claim: The exact failed step beyond the message.
outcomes.remediation: Retry only idempotent RPCs.
outcomes.notes: Messages differ from H1/H2 ('Backend unavailable', 'Resource exhausted', Internal=>14). v0.9.19 (#6777): native H3 backend (H3 frontend) connect timeout answers 4 'Backend deadline exceeded' instead of 14 (src/http3/server.rs:15130, :15161) and a backend TLS-config failure 13 'Internal gateway error' (src/http3/server.rs:15123). v0.9.19 (#6780, issue #6772): a client upload abort before headers is CANCELLED 'Client disconnected', a gateway-closed upload 14 'Request stream closed by the gateway', a malformed upload body 3 'Malformed request body', on the native H3 path and the H3-to-gRPC bridge (src/http3/server.rs:15148, :15150; src/http3/cross_protocol.rs:11199, :11203; src/proxy/client_abort.rs:107). v0.9.20 (#6976, #6979): a native H3 head failure observed after the dispatch or client deadline settles as that bound.

outcomes.condition: Native gRPC dispatch fails inside the gateway before any dial: the backend TLS client configuration cannot be built (e.g. unreadable backend CA/client cert material) or the backend URL, path or request authority is invalid. H1/H2 frontends and native HTTP/3 backends since v0.9.19; the HTTP/3-to-gRPC bridge already answered this way.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway reported an internal error preparing the gRPC backend call; nothing was sent to the backend.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend failed or was unreachable, or which configuration item is wrong.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: check the gateway log for the backend TLS material or backend URL error on this route. Do not retry as a transient outage.
outcomes.notes: New in v0.9.19 (#6777, issue #6773; commit tagged v0.9.18, unpublished): before, H1/H2 answered 14 'Backend unavailable' (protocol.grpc.backend_unavailable) and native HTTP/3 backends 14 'Service unavailable'. Health-neutral. Same text as protocol.grpc.response_build_failed, which uses 14.

outcomes.condition: Any gateway gRPC error for a gRPC-Web request; also backend responses lacking grpc-status on translated gRPC-Web.

public_signal.body_shape: gRPC-Web trailer frame (0x80 flag) carrying grpc-status/grpc-message; base64 for grpc-web-text
public_signal.transport: HTTP 200 with body-framed trailers [grpc-message: same mapping and messages as native gRPC]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: gRPC-Web errors arrive as HTTP 200 with a body-framed trailer carrying grpc-status.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Success from HTTP 200.
outcomes.remediation: Decode the trailer frame.
outcomes.notes: Backend-missing-status table differs: 400=>13, 401=>16, 403=>7, 404=>12, 429/502/503/504=>14, other (incl. 200)=>2. v0.9.20 (#6965): HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 pre-routing refusals (URL length, query count, protocol headers, Host/authority, canonical path, per-IP 429, 0-RTT 425, retired-listener 421, TRACE) now answer gRPC-Web with a framed trailer status as HTTP/3 already did (src/proxy/mod.rs:34784); header-size/count limits stay JSON 431 (protocol.grpc.header_limits_not_grpc_shaped). Untranslatable gRPC-Web requests are refused by the plugin since v0.9.19 (#6826, plugin.grpc_web outcomes). Builder and status mapping unchanged (src/plugins/grpc_web.rs:2226, :2603).

outcomes.condition: FERRUM_WEBSOCKET_MAX_CONNECTIONS (default 20000) or per-IP WebSocket limit reached.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused the WebSocket upgrade because its WebSocket connection limit (global or per client IP) is reached.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later; operator: WebSocket limits.
outcomes.notes: Global and per-IP limits send identical bytes; no X-Gateway-Error. v0.9.15 (#6079): the per-IP budget groups native IPv6 clients by FERRUM_PER_IP_IPV6_PREFIX (default /64; 128 restores per-address), so IPv6 clients that share a prefix share one budget; IPv4 and IPv4-mapped IPv6 stay per-address.

outcomes.condition: Origin header not in the route's allowed_ws_origins.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused the WebSocket upgrade because the Origin is not allowed for this route.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Authentication failure.
outcomes.remediation: Use an allowed Origin or ask the operator.

outcomes.condition: Credential expiry elapsed before the WebSocket upgrade completed.

other_headers.www-authenticate: <committing mechanism's challenge, e.g. Bearer error="invalid_token"; 'ferrum-edge' when none>

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The caller's credential expired before the WebSocket upgrade completed.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Invalid credential at submission.
outcomes.remediation: Refresh credentials.
outcomes.notes: v0.9.19 (#6779, issue #6774; first tagged v0.9.18): the 401 now carries WWW-Authenticate with the committing mechanism's challenge (src/plugins/utils/auth_flow.rs:969: Basic for basic/ldap, Bearer error="invalid_token" for jwt/jwks/introspection, ApiKey, hmac, ClientCertificate, WS-Security, OIDC session, else the generic 'ferrum-edge') on H1/H2 (src/proxy/mod.rs:16361, and after the backend handshake at :17461) and H3 (src/http3/websocket.rs:628). An initial response header policy may replace the challenge but not remove it on H3 (src/http3/websocket.rs:452). Status and body unchanged.

outcomes.condition: FERRUM_WEBSOCKET_MAX_LIFETIME_SECONDS (default 3600) elapsed before upgrade completed.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway's maximum WebSocket lifetime elapsed before the upgrade completed.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Retry; operator: lifetime settings.

outcomes.condition: Backend WebSocket dial or upgrade handshake fails with any class other than a timeout or a connection-ceiling refusal: DNS, TCP refused/reset, TLS, port exhaustion, a denied literal-IP backend, or the backend answered the upgrade with a non-101/200 status or protocol error. A connect or handshake timeout is upstream.connect.timeout (504) since v0.9.19.

public_signal.transport: HTTP response pre-upgrade; X-Gateway-Error connection_failure for a pre-wire dial failure (DNS, refused, TLS), backend_error when the backend received the upgrade and refused it (non-101/200, protocol error) or the gateway's egress policy denied the literal IP

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway could not establish the upstream WebSocket (connect/DNS/TLS failure or the backend refused the upgrade); the backend's own response is not shown.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Which of these happened, or that the backend is down (it may have answered the upgrade with an error).
outcomes.remediation: Operator: gateway logs; API owner: backend upgrade handling.
outcomes.notes: Backend's own rejection status/body is NOT relayed; no 504 variant; no X-Gateway-Error. H3 sends {"error":"DNS resolution for backend failed"} for DNS failures. v0.9.9 (#5875, PR #5877): an upgrade the gateway refuses by its own dial policy (unsafe Unix-socket authority, unparsable mesh target, denied literal-IP backend, unsupported backend TLS SNI override) is refused before an attempt begins; the client gets the same 502. v0.9.19 (#6777, issues #6770/#6773; first tagged v0.9.18): both WebSocket frontends take status and body from the shared mapper (src/proxy/mod.rs:16241 -> :50113) and stamp X-Gateway-Error (src/proxy/mod.rs:16214; H3 src/http3/websocket.rs:433). The earlier notes 'no 504 variant; no X-Gateway-Error' no longer hold: a timeout is now the 504 of upstream.connect.timeout. Token: connection_failure when !request_reached_wire (src/retry.rs:471) and the class is not DispatchPolicyRejected, else backend_error (a backend non-101 answer is WsError::Http -> RequestError, src/retry.rs:844). H3 still answers DNS failures with 502 {"error":"DNS resolution for backend failed"} (src/http3/websocket.rs:1528), now with X-Gateway-Error connection_failure. The mapper's BackendConnectionLimit arm (503 {"error":"Backend connection limit exceeded"} with X-Gateway-Error connection_failure) is reachable only if a WS dial error carries a backend_conn_limit refusal (src/retry.rs:1399); not settled for the WS dial paths.

outcomes.condition: DestinationRule maxConnections reached for the WebSocket backend.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused the upgrade because a gateway-configured backend connection ceiling is reached.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later; operator: maxConnections.
outcomes.notes: Same body as the reqwest HTTP lane but without X-Gateway-Error.

outcomes.condition: Gateway-internal WebSocket upgrade failure.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Internal server error during WebSocket upgrade"} | {"error":"Invalid backend path coordinates"} | {"error":"WebSocket request buffering invariant violated"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway failed internally during the WebSocket upgrade.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Operator: logs.

outcomes.condition: Circuit breaker open or adaptive_concurrency shed on a WebSocket upgrade (overload/config_stale pre-routing fences also apply).

public_signal.body_shape: the same JSON bodies as the HTTP admission outcomes

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused the WebSocket upgrade at an admission fence named by X-Gateway-Error; the upgrade was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later.
outcomes.notes: Only these four pre-upgrade WebSocket rejects carry X-Gateway-Error.

outcomes.condition: Gateway policy close mid-session: credential expired, maximum lifetime, client trust withdrawn, fragmented-message limit (FERRUM_WEBSOCKET_MAX_INCOMPLETE_MESSAGE_FRAMES 1024 / _SECONDS 60), ws_rate_limiting, WAF message block.

public_signal.transport: Close frame sent to both peers (bounded 100 ms write), then teardown [ws close reason: "credential expired | maximum lifetime reached | client trust withdrawn | fragmented message limit | <ws_rate_limiting close_reason, default 'Frame rate exceeded'> | message rejected by security policy | message exceeds inspectable size | message could not be inspected"]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway closed the WebSocket for a policy reason given in the close reason (credential/lifetime/trust, fragment limit, rate limit, or WAF).
outcomes.must_not_claim: An application-level error, or a policy other than the stated reason.
outcomes.remediation: Act on the close reason: refresh credentials, slow down, or change message content.
outcomes.notes: The reason string distinguishes the policy. Tunnel mode (FERRUM_WEBSOCKET_TUNNEL_MODE) sends no Close frame.

outcomes.condition: Gateway drain/shutdown or idle timeout (FERRUM_WEBSOCKET_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, default 300).

public_signal.transport: Close frame to both peers [ws close reason: 'gateway draining | idle timeout']

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway closed the WebSocket because it is draining or the session was idle.
outcomes.must_not_claim: An application error.
outcomes.remediation: Reconnect; send keepalives if idle.
outcomes.notes: A relay failure racing the drain also becomes 1001 'gateway draining'.

outcomes.condition: Frame > FERRUM_MAX_WEBSOCKET_FRAME_SIZE_BYTES (default 16 MiB) or message > 4x that; or a ws_message_size_limiting ceiling for the direction the frame travels (top-level max_frame_bytes / max_message_bytes, overridable per direction by client_to_backend / backend_to_client since v0.9.19); with websocket_permessage_deflate: terminate also a compressed frame or inflated frame/message over those ceilings or over FERRUM_WEBSOCKET_PERMESSAGE_DEFLATE_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES.

public_signal.transport: Close frame to both peers (either direction) [ws close reason: "'' (global limit) | <plugin close_reason, default 'Message too large'>"]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: A WebSocket frame or message exceeded a gateway size limit and the session was closed.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Protocol corruption, or which direction violated it without logs.
outcomes.remediation: Send smaller messages/frames.
outcomes.notes: Direction-dependent class: request_body_too_large (client->backend) or response_body_too_large (backend->client). v0.9.9 (#5769, PR #5869): with websocket_permessage_deflate: terminate a compressed frame past the frame ceiling, or a frame or message that inflates past it or past FERRUM_WEBSOCKET_PERMESSAGE_DEFLATE_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES (default 1 MiB), closes the session with 1009 and the reason 'compressed frame too large', 'decompressed frame too large' or 'decompressed message too large'. With passthrough the negotiated session is relayed as raw bytes and the gateway's frame and message bounds do not apply. v0.9.19 (#6881; first tagged v0.9.18): ws_message_size_limiting limits are directional (client_to_backend / backend_to_client override objects, each with its own close_reason; src/plugins/ws_message_size_limiting.rs:39) and the relay builds each framer's limits for its direction (src/proxy/mod.rs:20724). Under websocket_permessage_deflate: terminate a deflate size fault whose ceiling is exactly the binding plugin rule now closes with the plugin close_reason instead of 'compressed frame too large' / 'decompressed frame too large' / 'decompressed message too large' (src/proxy/mod.rs:20829-20856); the global or FERRUM_WEBSOCKET_PERMESSAGE_DEFLATE_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES ceilings keep the fixed reasons. v0.9.19 (#6940, issue #6912): on a Sidecar mesh H2 backend the 1009 Close is no longer lost in backend teardown (bounded 100 ms drain), so the backend leg now receives it as documented. Code 1009 unchanged.

outcomes.condition: Transport failure on either relay half (e.g. backend TCP reset / I/O error); since v0.9.20 also an H1/H2 client whose socket accepts no bytes for FERRUM_HTTP_CLIENT_WRITE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 60, 0 disables) while the gateway has bytes to write.

public_signal.transport: Close frame written to the surviving peer [ws close reason: 'relay error']

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway closed the WebSocket because relaying to the other side failed.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Which side failed or why.
outcomes.remediation: Reconnect; operator: logs.
outcomes.notes: Does not say which side failed. v0.9.20 (#6998): the client-write stall bound (src/proxy/client_write_stall.rs, armed at src/proxy/mod.rs:15622 and :25190) also covers upgraded WebSockets; per its module doc an upgraded session that stalls ends through the relay's own close path. The stalled client gets no Close frame it can read (client libraries report 1006); which Close the backend leg receives was not traced end to end (expected 1011 'relay error' from src/proxy/mod.rs:20938 for a non-protocol transport failure). HTTP/3 WebSockets are not covered.

outcomes.condition: RFC 6455 protocol violation by either peer.

public_signal.transport: Close frame to both peers [ws close reason: 'protocol error']

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway closed the WebSocket with a protocol error; a peer violated RFC 6455 (or, unverified, the backend dropped TCP without a Close handshake).
outcomes.must_not_claim: Which peer misbehaved.
outcomes.remediation: Check client and backend WebSocket framing.
outcomes.notes: Inferred, unverified: a backend TCP FIN without a Close handshake may surface in tungstenite as Protocol(ResetWithoutClosingHandshake) and therefore 1002 rather than 1011.

outcomes.condition: A peer (normally the backend) sends a Close frame.

public_signal.transport: peer Close code and reason forwarded verbatim

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: A Close code not in the gateway's set (1001/1002/1008/1009/1011 with the gateway's reasons) was relayed from the backend unchanged.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the gateway authored it.
outcomes.remediation: Interpret per the application's close codes.
outcomes.notes: If a gateway policy Close was already published, the policy Close wins.

outcomes.condition: FERRUM_WEBSOCKET_TUNNEL_MODE=true (H1/H2, no plugin that requires WebSocket framing; since v0.9.19 a bandwidth-priced api_chargeback instance also requires framing): lifetime, drain or trust stop.

public_signal.transport: raw transport dropped without a Close frame (client libraries typically report 1006)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The WebSocket transport ended without a Close frame.
outcomes.must_not_claim: A specific cause, or that 1006 was transmitted by a peer.
outcomes.remediation: Reconnect; operator: logs.
outcomes.notes: No size/fragment/WAF/rate closes in tunnel mode. v0.9.7 (#5588): server-first / reply bytes that a WSS (tokio-rustls) client leg accepted but could not yet encrypt under backpressure are flushed instead of held until the next write or the idle-timeout drop; tunnel mode arms no backend write timeout, so no new close path was added. v0.9.19 (#6842; first tagged v0.9.18): a bandwidth-priced api_chargeback instance requires WebSocket framing (src/plugins/api_chargeback.rs:3995), so its proxy's sessions stay on the parsed relay even with tunnel mode on and stop with the Close frames of the parsed relay (1008/1001) instead of a dropped transport.

outcomes.condition: RFC 9220 WebSocket over HTTP/3 when FERRUM_HTTP3_WEBSOCKET_ENABLED is false.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"WebSocket over HTTP/3 is disabled on this gateway"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: WebSocket over HTTP/3 is disabled on this gateway.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Use HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 WebSocket.

outcomes.condition: Gateway shutdown (HTTP/2 connections). Since v0.9.19 (#6781) the connection is closed when the shutdown drain wait ends, cutting streams still in flight.

public_signal.transport: GOAWAY; in-flight streams continue; new streams on the connection meanwhile get the overload 503 [h2: NO_ERROR (GOAWAY, hyper)]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The server announced graceful connection shutdown (GOAWAY NO_ERROR); streams above last-stream-id were not processed.
outcomes.must_not_claim: TLS failure or that in-flight streams failed.
outcomes.remediation: Open a new connection.
outcomes.notes: Library behaviour; FERRUM_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS (default 30) bounds the process drain. v0.9.19 (#6781, issue #6768): after GOAWAY the H1/H2 connection task also races the end of the drain wait (src/proxy/mod.rs:15811) and closes the connection then, so streams still running at FERRUM_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS are cut (no reason transmitted beyond the earlier GOAWAY). Before, the connection was polled until it completed.

outcomes.condition: Authenticated stream expired and the client did not drain the terminal, or client-cert trust withdrawn for the TLS connection. Since v0.9.19 (#6870) also: a gRPC RPC deadline (client grpc-timeout or grpc_deadline budget) fired on an H1/H2 response and the client did not drain the DEADLINE_EXCEEDED terminal within the 2 s grace.

public_signal.transport: GOAWAY then TCP hard close after 2 s (AUTHORIZATION_TRANSPORT_CLOSE_SETTLE, src/proxy/mod.rs:15912); sibling streams can die [h2: NO_ERROR (GOAWAY, hyper)]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The server sent GOAWAY and closed the connection.
outcomes.must_not_claim: A specific cause.
outcomes.remediation: Reconnect; if repeated with long streams, check credential expiry.
outcomes.notes: v0.9.19 (#6870): the gateway-owned gRPC deadline pump requests the same connection close when its terminal is not drained within TRANSPORT_CLOSE_GRACE (2 s, src/proxy/response_watchdog.rs:193, request at :458), so a gRPC client that withholds flow-control credit past its deadline can see its whole connection (and sibling streams) closed. v0.9.20 (#6982) keeps the expiry and grace for responses already complete.

outcomes.condition: Client opens more concurrent streams than advertised SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS.

public_signal.transport: QUIC handshake refused [h3: QUIC transport CONNECTION_REFUSED (quinn Incoming::refuse)]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The QUIC handshake was refused by the server, consistent with gateway overload or drain.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Network blocking with certainty.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later or fall back to TCP.
outcomes.notes: Library code. v0.9.15 (#6085): handshakes from unvalidated sources run inside a per-listener budget (FERRUM_HTTP3_MAX_UNVALIDATED_HANDSHAKES, default 1024; src/http3/address_validation.rs:99); past it the source gets a stateless Retry (one extra round trip), and an Initial that already followed a Retry is refused without a handshake. The listener and backend pools no longer advertise QUIC DATAGRAM, and a peer that sends a DATAGRAM frame is closed with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (src/http3/config.rs:440); CONNECT-UDP carries HTTP Datagrams as capsules on the request stream.

outcomes.notes: v0.9.19 (#6779): every built-in mechanism advertises a challenge and the 401 lists all applicable ones (src/proxy/mod.rs:33347 missing_authentication_reject; render_authentication_challenges joins them with ', '). Exception: jwks_auth mesh permissive-missing-token metadata with exactly one applicable auth plugin lets the request through. On proxies whose chain has ai_federation/ai_stream_router the body is replaced (proxy.auth_phase.openai_envelope_missing). A jwks DPoP proof is already consumed when the no-identity path is taken. gRPC: HTTP 200 trailers-only, grpc-status 16, grpc-message 'Authentication required', WWW-Authenticate kept as a header. WS: ordinary 401 on the upgrade request. Public reason detail: None; does not name the mechanisms tried. Distinguishability: Same body as plugin.oidc_relying_party.challenge_api_* (those carry 'Bearer realm="oidc", error="invalid_token"'). 'WWW-Authenticate: ferrum-edge' is the gateway's generic fallback on any gateway 401 whose route has no applicable mechanism (src/plugins/utils/auth_flow.rs:610); on a route with any built-in auth plugin it no longer appears. gRPC status derived from src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:3132 mapping. v0.9.15 (#6090): HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/3 ingress remove the fields a client's Connection header nominates before any plugin runs (src/proxy/headers.rs:550; src/proxy/mod.rs:35453, src/http3/server.rs:3576), keeping only Host, Content-Length, Expect and the forwarding fields, so a request that sends Connection: authorization reaches this 401 on an authenticated route. HTTP/2 rejects Connection and is unchanged.

Distinguishability: Identical to mesh_ext_authz check_failed_closed at default statusOnError=403 and to provider denials that return 403 without forwarded headers. gRPC status derived from src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:3132 mapping. v0.9.9 (#5948, PR #5950): on a route that allows ';' path parameters (MeshService.allow_path_parameters or ferrum.io/allow-path-parameters, #5947) every rule is judged on the raw and the parameter-stripped path: DENY, CUSTOM and AUDIT match on either spelling, ALLOW only on both, so '/admin;x/users' now meets a DENY on '/admin/*' and this 403 is answered more often there. Routes without the opt-in refuse ';' earlier with gateway.routing.path_parameter_refused (400). connection.sni conditions are normalized (trailing dot, case, IDNA A-label) and the received SNI loses one trailing dot before policy, so a DENY on admin.example.com now also fires for 'admin.example.com.' (#5903). A to.headers rule on a pseudo-header (':path', ':method', ':authority', ':scheme') is refused at config validation instead of never matching (#5951, PR #5952). The public signal is unchanged. v0.9.15 (issue #6081 / #6083): a byte-stream or datagram HBONE CONNECT relay, including a bare authenticated HTTP/2 CONNECT on the Sidecar inbound listener, is authorized as a Layer-4 session (src/plugins/mesh/authz.rs:3766): to.operation methods, paths, hosts and headers, requestPrincipals and when: request.headers[...] / request.auth.* are unobservable, so a DENY rule ignores them and matches on its remaining constraints, an ALLOW or AUDIT rule that needs one never matches, and a matched CUSTOM rule refuses the relay with this 403 without calling the provider. An L7 rule that selects a workload reached over HBONE therefore refuses the whole tunnel; the public signal does not say which rule. v0.9.19 (#6825, commit first tagged v0.9.18): to.headers, when: request.headers[...] and the headers sent to a CUSTOM provider read every field line of a repeated header joined the way the gateway materializes it (src/plugins/mesh/authz.rs:1426), so 'x-tenant: ok' + 'x-tenant: banned' now meets a DENY that used to see only the first line; header case variants are canonicalized first (#6932, authz.rs:3576). Flat mesh_policies / embedded mesh_slice config with never-matching matchers (pseudo-header to.headers, bad host/port patterns, empty from/to entries, empty name/namespace) is refused at plugin construction (authz.rs:2195) instead of loading a DENY that never fires. v0.9.19 (#6809): on a NodeWaypoint with per_pod_policy_scoping, the destination pod's own AuthorizationPolicy (node_waypoint_capture_mesh_policies) is evaluated for capture relays, so DENY / implicit-deny from the destination namespace now produce this 403 where they were not enforced before. v0.9.20 (#6961): destination-scope lookups are keyed by namespace and upstream id (authz.rs:2795), so colliding generated upstream ids across namespaces no longer borrow each other's policy scope. outcomes.notes: Header names are lowercase x-ratelimit-limit / x-ratelimit-remaining / x-ratelimit-window; there are NO RateLimit-* (IETF) or Retry-After headers. When several rate_limiting instances are composed, the refusing instance owns the published header set. Native gRPC: rendered by normalize_reject_response_with_provenance (src/proxy/mod.rs:29222) as HTTP 200, content-type application/grpc, trailers-only; grpc-status mapped from HTTP status via http_reject_status_to_grpc_status (src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:3132); grpc-message = body JSON 'error' value. 429 -> grpc-status 8 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, grpc-message 'Rate limit exceeded'; x-ratelimit-* kept in the trailers-only header map. WebSocket: refused at the upgrade handshake as a plain HTTP 429. TCP/UDP: see plugin.rate_limiting.stream_refused. Public reason detail: No limiter key/identity is exposed (x-ratelimit-identity is stripped from requests and responses). Limit and window are exposed only when expose_headers=true. Distinguishability: Same body as the local-capacity 429 (which never carries x-ratelimit-* headers). Different body from graphql 429 ({"errors":[...]}), grpc_method_router 429 and ai_rate_limiter. No Retry-After header is ever set by this plugin. gRPC status derived from src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:3132 mapping. v0.9.7 Redis-mode counting (rate_limiting/graphql/grpc_method_router request quotas, src/plugins/utils/rate_limit.rs:2726 check_http_windows_redis): each window is 16 sub-buckets; a decision sums the charged sub-bucket, the 17 before it and the one after (each at face value, floored at 0), charges every window in one MULTI/EXEC ending in TIME, refuses when the count including this request exceeds the limit (:2878), and hands the charge back on EVERY window after a refusal (:2911), so refused requests no longer consume budget (the v0.9.5 multi-window phantom increment is gone) and a burst at the end of a window is counted in full. Consequence: a client sending at exactly its configured rate is throttled to at least limit/(limit+ceil(3*limit/16)) admitted (50% at limit 1, 80% at 8); v0.9.5 used a two-window weighted estimate (different boundary timing). Redis counters move to new keys ({prefix:rate-key}:{window_seconds}:{sub_index}), so an in-place upgrade restarts counting (up to one window of reduced enforcement; mixed-version replicas count separately). During a Redis outage the v0.9.7 default (redis_failure_policy=local_fallback) produces this same 429 from a per-process budget instead of the v0.9.5 default 503. v0.9.9 (#5908, PR #5943): with mcp_tool_calls configured the limiter counts MCP tools/call members instead and answers a refusal as a JSON-RPC error on HTTP 200 (plugin.rate_limiting.mcp_tool_calls_exceeded, plugin.rate_limiting.mcp_tool_calls_unavailable, plugin.rate_limiting.mcp_uninspectable_encoding); this 429 body is unchanged for every other request. v0.9.15 (#6079): IP keys group IPv6 clients by the policy's new ipv6_prefix (1-128, default 64; 128 restores per-address keys); FERRUM_PER_IP_IPV6_PREFIX does not apply. IPv6 counters (local and Redis) restart once on upgrade. v0.9.19 (#6814): every quota 429 now carries Retry-After (src/plugins/rate_limiting.rs:812), whether or not expose_headers is set: exact for the local token bucket and sliding aggregate (src/plugins/utils/rate_limit.rs:2405), a conservative bound of at most 19/16 of the window in Redis mode (src/plugins/utils/rate_limit.rs:2493, :2916), the longest wait over every refusing window. This supersedes the earlier statements that the plugin never sets Retry-After. The local-capacity 429 and the MCP JSON-RPC refusals carry none, so Retry-After now separates a quota 429 from the capacity 429. limit_by=service (src/plugins/rate_limiting.rs:1703, :734) adds an aggregate per-policy budget.
