outcomes.condition: Non-gRPC request on a mesh_route_dispatch rule with request_timeout_ms (Gateway API HTTPRoute rules[].timeouts.request projects onto it); the total deadline expired while an attempt that had already been handed to the backend (after buffered client-body collection, request-body hooks, DNS and backend admission) was still waiting for the response head or for buffered response-body collection. The attempt is cancelled (RouteDeadlineExpiry::InFlight with the handoff marker set; every retry attempt counts as handed over from its first poll).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge reports the route's total request deadline (HTTPRoute timeouts.request / mesh_route_dispatch request_timeout_ms) ran out before a response head was available; the response does not say which phase used the time or whether the backend received the request.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend was slow or received the request (the deadline also spans gateway-side phases, the client upload and retry backoff), which phase expired, the configured duration, or that the request is safe to replay.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator / API owner: compare the rule's timeouts.request with backend latency plus client upload time and retry backoff; the gateway transaction log records metadata route_request_timeout = dispatch | before_dispatch | retry_backoff (src/plugins/mod.rs:284, :5481). Retry only idempotent requests.
outcomes.notes: v0.9.6+ only (no route deadline exists at v0.9.5). X-Gateway-Error comes from status 504 (src/retry.rs:301); from v0.9.8 the sibling that no backend held carries request_timeout instead (upstream.route_request_timeout.not_dispatched), so on this release backend_timeout on this body means a backend held the attempt. Enforced on native HTTP/3 and the HTTP/3 bridge too (v0.9.8, #5646, #5729). Never retried. Error_class read_write_timeout (charged to the backend). On HTTP/1.1 / HTTP/2 built with an empty header map, so no Content-Type. v0.9.11: request_on_wire is tracked separately from health-neutral classification. The same route_timeout phase decides request_timeout before backend handoff versus backend_timeout during dispatch; per-attempt budgets remain separate. A native-H3 HEADERS-completion marker does not identify partial first-wire submission, so lifetime expiry never licenses replay.

source.symbol: RouteDeadlineExpiry::phase (before_dispatch unless handed to a backend)
native HTTP/3 early route upload phase

outcomes.condition: Non-gRPC request on a mesh_route_dispatch rule with request_timeout_ms (Gateway API timeouts.request), over HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 or (new in v0.9.8) native HTTP/3; the total deadline (anchored at receipt) expired before any attempt was handed to a backend - already spent when the attempt would start, or while the gateway was still collecting a buffered client upload, running request-body hooks, resolving DNS or waiting for backend admission - or while the gateway slept in retry backoff after a failed attempt. From v0.9.13 the total also bounds a body collected before before_proxy (body-before-auth plugins such as soap_ws_security, hmac_auth, waf) when the rule can be previewed from the pinned matchers.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge reports the route's total request deadline (HTTPRoute timeouts.request / mesh_route_dispatch request_timeout_ms) ran out before any backend held this attempt; it does not say which gateway-side phase used the time.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That a backend was slow or received this attempt, which phase expired, the configured duration, or that the request is safe to replay. In the retry-backoff case an earlier attempt did reach a backend.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator / API owner: compare the rule's timeouts.request with client upload time, gateway-side processing and retry backoff; the gateway transaction log records metadata route_request_timeout = before_dispatch | retry_backoff (HTTP/3 upload: rejection phase route_request_timeout_h3_upload; early body collection from v0.9.13: route_request_timeout_early_upload). Retry only idempotent requests.
outcomes.notes: v0.9.8 (#5762, #5778): this 504 carries X-Gateway-Error: request_timeout; v0.9.7 sent backend_timeout here, which blamed a backend that never saw the request. The token comes from x_gateway_error_for_response (src/proxy/mod.rs:28709), which reads a typed marker only trusted proxy code sets (a plugin writing the route_request_timeout metadata key cannot change it, #5783). Body bytes are identical to upstream.route_request_timeout.backend_held; the token tells them apart. Native HTTP/3 (and the HTTP/3 bridge) now enforce the rule instead of refusing it: the same 504 and token; a deadline that fires while an HTTP/3 upload is still buffered is answered as a plugin-style reject with Content-Type application/json and logged under rejection phase route_request_timeout_h3_upload (src/http3/server.rs:20109). On HTTP/1.1 / HTTP/2 it is built with an empty header map (no Content-Type). Never retried; health-neutral (error_class dispatch_policy_rejected). gRPC-flavoured requests never get this body: the route budget is folded into the RPC deadline and ends with DEADLINE_EXCEEDED. No route deadline exists at v0.9.5. v0.9.11: request_on_wire is tracked separately from health-neutral classification. The same route_timeout phase decides request_timeout before backend handoff versus backend_timeout during dispatch; per-attempt budgets remain separate. A native-H3 HEADERS-completion marker does not identify partial first-wire submission, so lifetime expiry never licenses replay. v0.9.13 (#6008): an early (pre-before_proxy) collection that outlives a previewed route total ends with this 504, X-Gateway-Error request_timeout and Content-Type application/json on HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and native HTTP/3, logged before_dispatch under rejection phase route_request_timeout_early_upload; health-neutral. An undetermined rule uses the largest candidate total, and any untimed candidate leaves only the read/RPC bounds. gRPC folds the previewed total into DEADLINE_EXCEEDED.

outcomes.condition: Non-gRPC request on a mesh_route_dispatch rule with attempt_timeout_ms (Gateway API timeouts.backendRequest projects onto both attempt_timeout_ms and timeout_ms); the attempt's budget, started when the attempt was handed to the backend (after buffered client-body collection, request-body hooks, DNS and admission; for a streamed upload the upload time after handoff counts), expired before the response head or before buffered response-body collection finished, while the route's total deadline had not.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge reports the upstream did not complete its part of the exchange within the gateway's backend timeout budget; the request may have been partially or fully delivered.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Which direction stalled (upload write vs response header wait vs buffered body idle), that the backend definitely received the full request, or that raising timeouts is the fix, or whether a route per-attempt budget or backend_read_timeout_ms fired.
outcomes.remediation: API owner: check backend latency for this operation; gateway operator: check backend_read_timeout_ms / backend_write_timeout_ms for the route. Retry only idempotent requests. For Gateway API routes check the rule's timeouts.backendRequest.
outcomes.notes: v0.9.6+ only. Byte-identical to the backend_read_timeout_ms 504 (same builder, connection_error=false); which bound fired is in gateway logs only. Charged to the backend. Retryable like any 504: each retry gets a fresh budget; Gateway API retry replays it only if 504 is in codes and the method is GET/HEAD/OPTIONS/PUT/DELETE (src/config_sources/k8s/gateway_api.rs:7272, src/config/types.rs:2777, src/retry.rs:1970), always within the total timeouts.request. gRPC folds the budget into its RPC deadline (gRPC slice); native HTTP/3 refuses such rules with 503 (H3 slice). After the head, the same budget cuts the body (streaming.route_deadline_cut_after_headers). No Content-Type header on the HTTP/1.1 / HTTP/2 backend-response path: the gateway builds this body with an empty header map (lab-observed over HTTP/1.1 on 0.9.5 and 0.9.7: UP-009, UP-010; the v0.9.5 audit had recorded application/json). The HTTP/3 writer was not lab-checked. v0.9.8: native HTTP/3 and the HTTP/3 bridge enforce the budget too (src/http3/route_deadline.rs:185), start a fresh budget for each retry attempt and retry an expiry when the rule's retry lists 504 (#5743); the HTTP/3 bridge also collects a buffered response body inside the attempt when a failure there could be retried (#5738). v0.9.11: request_on_wire is tracked separately from health-neutral classification. The same route_timeout phase decides request_timeout before backend handoff versus backend_timeout during dispatch; per-attempt budgets remain separate. A native-H3 HEADERS-completion marker does not identify partial first-wire submission, so lifetime expiry never licenses replay.

source.symbol: TotalDeadlineBody::size_hint keeps exact hint for error-only deadlines
route deadline cut settles backend accounting health-neutrally

outcomes.condition: Non-gRPC streaming response (status and headers already sent) on a rule with request_timeout_ms and/or attempt_timeout_ms (Gateway API timeouts.request / timeouts.backendRequest): the earlier of the total deadline (from receipt) and the committed attempt's budget (from handoff) elapsed before the body finished. Applies to healthy large downloads, SSE and long polls as well as trickling backends. Buffered (Full) responses are never cut here (a deadline during buffered collection yields the 504 outcomes).

public_signal.transport: Body ends with a TimedOut transport error, never a clean EOF: HTTP/2 stream reset (hyper; RST_STREAM code is library behaviour), HTTP/1.1 connection closed. The wrapper keeps the inner body's exact size hint (src/proxy/body.rs:5986), so a response whose length was known keeps Content-Length framing and the cut shows as a body shorter than Content-Length; an unknown-length body ends without the terminating 0-chunk. No trailer or marker is synthesized. HTTP/3 (v0.9.8): the stream is reset with H3_REQUEST_CANCELLED, never finished cleanly.
public_signal.x_gateway_error_note: only if status>=500 was already sent

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Response headers arrived but the response body did not complete; the transfer was cut by the gateway or upstream after the status was sent.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the response is complete or successful because the status was 2xx, that the backend stalled (a route deadline also ends healthy long responses), which cause applied, or that a non-idempotent request is safe to replay.
outcomes.remediation: Treat the result as incomplete; retry only idempotent requests; gateway operator: size the route's timeouts.request / timeouts.backendRequest for the longest complete response the rule must serve and correlate gateway logs (body_error_class read_write_timeout).
outcomes.notes: v0.9.6+ only. Never retried (head already committed). Health-neutral for the backend; the deferred log keeps body_error_class read_write_timeout without a client-disconnect flag. gRPC requests fold the deadlines into the RPC deadline instead (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED trailers, gRPC slice); the native HTTP/3 frontend never serves such rules. v0.9.8: native HTTP/3 and the HTTP/3 bridge cut a response still streaming at either deadline, including one whose client withholds QUIC flow control (every downstream write races the deadline, #5741); the cut is health-neutral (body_error_class read_write_timeout). A buffered response is complete when written and is not cut. v0.9.20 (#6973, issue #6022): a backend body error observed at or after the route deadline is settled as this health-neutral cut, not as streaming.backend_body_failure_after_headers (src/proxy/body.rs:5956). The client-visible cut is the same.

source.symbol: plaintext listener wraps the client socket
RST_STREAM(CANCEL) on a closed-window response stall

outcomes.condition: An HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 proxy client stops taking response bytes while the gateway has bytes to write, for FERRUM_HTTP_CLIENT_WRITE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 60, 0 disables, max 86400). Transport stall (the socket accepts no bytes; HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, upgraded WebSockets): the whole client connection is closed. HTTP/2 flow-control stall (h2c and ALPN h2 frontends: a stream has a response chunk ready and the client grants it no window): that stream is reset. Time spent waiting on a slow backend never counts, and any accepted write re-arms the bound. HTTP/3 and admin listeners are not covered.

public_signal.transport: HTTP/1.1: the gateway closes the client connection, so a streamed body ends without its terminating 0-chunk or short of Content-Length (or no response head arrives if the head itself was never accepted). HTTP/2 transport stall: the connection closes and every stream on it fails. HTTP/2 window stall: RST_STREAM(CANCEL) on that stream only; the connection and its other streams continue. No trailer, marker or X-Gateway-Error is written.
public_signal.x_gateway_error_note: only if status>=500 was already sent

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The response did not complete; the connection or stream was cut after the client stopped accepting response data for a long period. A client-side read stall, rather than an upstream fault, is the likely cause when the client knows it paused reading.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend failed or was slow, that the response was complete, that the cut came from the gateway rather than a network path when the client did not observe its own stall, or that a non-idempotent request is safe to replay.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: keep reading the response (or grant HTTP/2 flow-control window) while downloading; gateway operator: raise FERRUM_HTTP_CLIENT_WRITE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, or set 0, for workloads that legitimately pause reading for over a minute.
outcomes.notes: New in v0.9.20 (#6998 transport bound, #7005 HTTP/2 window bound). The gateway logs error_kind=client_write_stall at info (src/proxy/mod.rs:15870; TLS listeners :25551). The bound is nginx's send_timeout analogue and sits below rustls on TLS listeners (src/proxy/mod.rs:25190). The transaction's body_error_class for a stalled response was not settled by reading. A request still waiting on a slow backend is never cut by this bound.

source.symbol: relay synthesis: a peerless CONNECT gets the unauthenticated-peer 403 (v0.9.8)

outcomes.condition: Mesh inbound HBONE CONNECT (byte or datagram tunnel) whose peer is not admitted: no authenticated mesh peer identity (v0.9.5 and later), or, new in v0.9.6+, an authenticated peer whose retained certificate chain no longer verifies against the inbound admission trust in force (trust bundle rotation) or is revoked by the enforced CRL set. Refused before any upstream is selected or dialed. From v0.9.8 also a CONNECT with no verified SPIFFE identity that relay synthesis refuses (an authority the terminator does not own): it gets this 403, not a destination denial, so an unauthenticated peer learns nothing about destination ownership (#5763).

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"HBONE tunnel requires an authenticated mesh peer"} | {"error":"HBONE UDP tunnel requires an authenticated mesh peer"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The destination gateway did not admit the mesh peer for an HBONE tunnel (missing authenticated identity, or a credential no longer trusted/valid there).
outcomes.must_not_claim: Which admission check failed (identity missing, trust anchor, or revocation): the bodies are byte-identical by design; the cause is only in the destination's log (mesh_authz.deny_policy / rejection phase).
outcomes.remediation: Mesh operator: check the peer's SVID, trust bundle distribution and CRLs on the destination; destination log reason hbone_unauthenticated_peer | hbone_peer_trust_withdrawn | hbone_peer_revoked (udp: hbone_udp_*).
outcomes.notes: Mesh-only (peer is another mesh proxy, not an API client). The bodies are NOT new in v0.9.7: v0.9.5 already emitted them for an unauthenticated peer (v0.9.5 hbone_proxy.rs:907 / 1216); v0.9.7 adds the credential-admission trigger (#5568/#5574) with the identical body. The drift entry 'HBONE tunnels without an authenticated mesh peer now 403' overstates the change. Successful CONNECT 200s may now carry x-ferrum-mesh-tunnel-reuse: fenced (src/proxy/hbone_proxy.rs:1743; capability only, spoofable marker).

source.symbol: post-DNS screen of the resolved destination

outcomes.condition: Mesh inbound HBONE CONNECT (byte or datagram tunnel) from an authenticated mesh peer whose destination this terminator does not own or does not declare: refused at relay synthesis (new in v0.9.8, #5763; before, a 404 route miss), at the post-plugin re-check after a route override moved the destination, at the post-DNS screen of the resolved destination, or (since v0.9.17, #6125) a bare byte-stream CONNECT on the Sidecar inbound listener that matched a route serving HTTP (reason http_application_port).

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"HBONE relay destination not allowed"} | {"error":"HBONE UDP relay destination not allowed"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The destination mesh proxy refused to relay this HBONE tunnel to the requested destination; it does not relay to destinations it does not own.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Which relay check refused it (not owned, undeclared port, unresolvable, ingress mapping): the body is identical; the reason is only in the destination's transaction log (mesh.relay.denial_reason).
outcomes.remediation: Mesh operator: check which proxy terminates the destination and that the workload declares the port; the destination's transaction line carries mesh_authz.deny_policy hbone_relay_destination_denied (udp: hbone_udp_relay_destination_denied), mesh.relay.denial_reason and mesh.relay.denied_destination.
outcomes.notes: Mesh-only (the peer is another mesh proxy, not an API client). The body existed at v0.9.7 for the post-plugin re-check and the post-DNS screens but was uncatalogued there; v0.9.7 answered a relay-synthesis refusal with gateway.routing.no_route's 404 (lab MESH-009/010/011/023/028/033). v0.9.8 also counts datagram re-check and post-DNS refusals as relay_destination_denied and brackets an IPv6 mesh.relay.denied_destination. A peerless CONNECT gets protocol.hbone.connect_peer_not_admitted instead, and a terminator without its first mesh slice protocol.hbone.relay_not_ready. v0.9.17 (#6125, issue #6110): a Sidecar-inbound bare CONNECT that matches an HTTP-family route is refused before the route's plugins with the same 403 relay-denied answer as a route-miss relay to an HTTP application port (src/proxy/mod.rs:36216, src/proxy/mod.rs:2748, predicate src/proxy/mod.rs:2734), so HTTP traffic cannot bypass the route's HTTP policy through a tunnel. v0.9.20 (#6969): an HBONE CONNECT that declares a gRPC or gRPC-Web Content-Type is refused earlier with plain 400 {"error":"gRPC requires POST method"} (src/proxy/mod.rs:35722; gateway.routing.grpc_requires_post, slice A_core).

outcomes.condition: Mesh inbound HBONE CONNECT (byte or datagram tunnel) from an authenticated mesh peer that reaches a terminator which has not applied its first mesh slice yet (denial reason no_mesh_slice), at relay synthesis, the handler re-checks or the post-DNS screens. New in v0.9.8 (#5763); v0.9.7 answered a 404 at synthesis and a 403 destination denial at the re-checks.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"HBONE relay not ready"} | {"error":"HBONE UDP relay not ready"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The destination mesh proxy is not ready to relay HBONE tunnels yet (it has no mesh configuration applied); retrying later may succeed.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the destination is not allowed or that the peer's identity was rejected.
outcomes.remediation: Mesh operator: check that the destination proxy receives its mesh configuration (control plane or file source); its transaction line carries mesh_authz.deny_policy hbone_relay_not_ready (udp: hbone_udp_relay_not_ready).
outcomes.notes: Mesh-only. Not counted as a relay_destination_denied rejection, so on v0.9.8 a 403 always means a real authorization denial. No X-Gateway-Error.

outcomes.condition: Mesh inbound HBONE: an established byte or datagram tunnel is cut by the admission-fence sweep that runs on config/trust/CRL/PeerAuthentication publications when the tunnel would no longer be admitted (proxy_withdrawn, peer_expired, peer_trust, peer_revoked, authorization_denied, peer_auth_transport, relay_destination, reuse_withdrawn, reevaluation_failed).

public_signal.transport: v0.9.9: the CONNECT stream is reset with RST_STREAM(CONNECT_ERROR) (byte and datagram tunnels, #5858, PR #5863); v0.9.8 and earlier ended it without a reason (a clean END_STREAM)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The mesh tunnel ended without an in-band reason; the destination may have revoked its admission after a policy or credential change.
outcomes.must_not_claim: A specific revocation reason or that the backend failed.
outcomes.remediation: Mesh operator: destination log 'HBONE tunnel closed: admission revoked' with reason; reconnect opens a fresh CONNECT under current policy.
outcomes.notes: New in v0.9.6+ (issue #5042 step 1). v0.9.5 tunnels outlived later policy/trust changes. Byte-tunnel first failure is a ConnectionAborted io error with message 'HBONE tunnel terminated: mesh admission revoked by a later policy generation' (classified connection_closed, src/retry.rs:967); the datagram relay logs body_error_class connection_closed. v0.9.8 (#5765): a datagram relay that ends on a socket error is recorded as an error with hbone.udp.termination_reason (src/proxy/hbone_proxy.rs:242); the client still sees a clean HTTP/2 END_STREAM. v0.9.9 (#5781/#5858, PRs #5856, #5863, vendored hyper 1.9.0 Upgraded::reset_with_connect_error): every relay ending except a peer close or an idle expiry resets the CONNECT stream with RST_STREAM(CONNECT_ERROR): a revocation, a socket error on either side (a backend that resets the connection, a datagram relay's tunnel_read_error / tunnel_write_error / app_send_error / app_recv_error), a backend read or write deadline, a datagram write stall and the TCP half-close cap. The client can now tell a cut tunnel from a complete one, but the reset code is the same for every cause, so the specific reason stays operator-log only. v0.9.15 (#6087): a live tunnel admitted on a view that a reload makes omit the route's authentication or admission policy (gateway.routing.protocol_not_permitted) is revoked with authorization_denied (src/proxy/hbone_admission_fence.rs:2142); a relay re-evaluation now authorizes the tunnel as a Layer-4 session (issue #6081 / #6083). v0.9.19 (#6873): the fence re-reads the tunnel's mapped Consumer from the generation it judges; a deleted Consumer (src/proxy/hbone_admission_fence.rs:2157) or one no longer allowed by the authorize chain revokes the live tunnel with authorization_denied. v0.9.17 (#6125): a reload that turns a tunnel's matched route into an HTTP route on the Sidecar inbound listener revokes it (relay_destination, src/proxy/hbone_admission_fence.rs:2218). Wire signal unchanged: RST_STREAM(CONNECT_ERROR).

source.symbol: connect failure: kernel ETIMEDOUT -> 504 Backend HBONE connection timed out
connect failure -> 502 Backend HBONE connection failed
connect timer -> 504 Backend HBONE connection timed out

outcomes.condition: Mesh inbound HBONE byte-stream CONNECT that was admitted and routed, but the terminator's own dial to the destination workload fails before the tunnel is established: DNS failure (502 DNS body), TCP connect refused/reset/unreachable (502), or connect timeout, either the gateway's backend_connect_timeout_ms timer or (since v0.9.19, #6777) a kernel ETIMEDOUT (504).

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Backend HBONE connection failed"} | {"error":"Backend HBONE connection timed out"} | {"error":"DNS resolution for backend failed"}
public_signal.transport: HTTP/2 CONNECT response (no tunnel established); no X-Gateway-Error on this reject path. 502 with the connection-failed or DNS body; 504 with the timed-out body.

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The destination mesh proxy could not connect to its local workload for this HBONE tunnel (connect failure or timeout); the tunnel was not established.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the peer's identity or authorization was refused, or that the workload received any tunnel bytes.
outcomes.remediation: Mesh operator / workload owner: check that the destination workload listens on the target port and is reachable from its mesh proxy; check backend_connect_timeout_ms (DestinationRule connect_timeout_ms).
outcomes.notes: New in v0.9.19 for the kernel-ETIMEDOUT 504 (#6777, issue #6770): before, a connect that failed with ETIMEDOUT (connect budget longer than the OS TCP timeout) answered the 502. The three bodies themselves predate v0.9.15 (v0.9.15 hbone_proxy.rs:739/:750) and were never catalogued. error_class varies: connection_timeout for the 504, connection_refused/connection_reset/dns_lookup_error for the 502s. The DNS body is shared with other upstream DNS failures. Flagged as a candidate for this slice by F_mesh_lab (drift hbone_backend_connect_etimedout_504).

outcomes.condition: Introspection provider answered active=true (and passed the cnf, token_type, issuer and audience checks) but returned an integer nbf later than the gateway clock (no leeway). Checked before exp, so it also wins over an elapsed exp. Such responses are never cached; positive-cache hits re-check the window. A JSON null nbf is treated as absent; a non-integer nbf is 503 introspection_unavailable instead.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: If the response came from a Ferrum Edge gateway, its oauth2_introspection plugin produced this outcome; the condition is: Introspection provider answered active=true (and passed the cnf, token_type, issuer and audience checks) but returned an integer nbf later than the gateway clock (no leeway). Checked before exp, so it also wins over an elapsed exp. Such responses are never cached; positive-cache hits re-check the window. A JSON null nbf is treated as absent; a non-integer nbf is 503 introspection_unavailable instead.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend application produced this response (unless the destination is not a trusted Ferrum endpoint, in which case the body alone proves nothing); that the token is revoked or inactive (the provider reported it active); whether the token was pre-minted or the authorization server and gateway clocks disagree.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: retry after the token's not-before time; if it persists, the operator should check clock synchronization between the authorization server and the gateway (no leeway is applied).
outcomes.notes: New in v0.9.7 (issue #5523); no such body in v0.9.5, which ignored introspection nbf. In fan-out mode a candidate's unavailability (503) outranks this decision, and the first auth decision among candidates wins. Public reason detail: not-yet-valid window. Distinguishability: Unique body. gRPC status derived from src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:3132 mapping.

outcomes.condition: Provider sets accept_mtls_bound_tokens, the introspection response is active with cnf exactly {"x5t#S256": <non-empty string>} and passes the token_type, issuer, audience and time checks, but the request has no verified frontend client certificate or its base64url SHA-256 thumbprint differs. Re-checked on every request, cache hits and coalesced lookups included, before any cached scope/role verdict.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: If the response came from a Ferrum Edge gateway, its oauth2_introspection plugin (or jwks_auth, which sends the same signal) refused an active certificate-bound token because the connection did not present the bound client certificate.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the token is inactive, expired or revoked; that the introspection service is down; whether the certificate was missing or different (both collapse); that the backend produced this response.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: send the request over a TLS connection presenting the client certificate the token is bound to (cnf.x5t#S256), or obtain a token bound to the certificate in use; do not retry unchanged.
outcomes.notes: New in v0.9.19 (#6840; tag v0.9.18 was not published, first released in v0.9.19). Default off (accept_mtls_bound_tokens false, src/plugins/oauth2_introspection.rs:396); without it any non-null cnf is plugin.oauth2_introspection.sender_constrained_unsupported. Same body and Bearer challenge as jwks_auth's mtls_binding_mismatch. In a multi-auth chain the field also lists other applicable challenges (src/proxy/mod.rs:33448). gRPC status derived from src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:3132 mapping.

outcomes.condition: REGISTRY_ONLY egress (auto-injected __mesh_outbound_registry scoped to the outbound capture listener ports, or an operator-configured mesh_outbound_registry, unscoped by default) and the HTTP-family request's Host/:authority host[:port] is not in the registry (bare host, host:port, host:*, or one-label *.suffix wildcard), on a listener not stamped Inbound.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: If the response came from a Ferrum Edge gateway, its mesh_outbound_registry plugin refused the request before dispatch; the condition is: REGISTRY_ONLY egress (auto-injected __mesh_outbound_registry scoped to the outbound capture listener ports, or an operator-configured mesh_outbound_registry, unscoped by default) and the HTTP-family request's Host/:authority host[:port] is not in the registry (bare host, host:port, host:*, or one-label *.suffix wildcard), on a listener not stamped Inbound.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the destination or backend is down or was contacted (nothing was dispatched); that credentials are invalid; that the body proves a Ferrum gateway produced it (backend-spoofable).
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: register the destination (Service/ServiceEntry or registry entry, including the port the client uses) or relax outboundTrafficPolicy; the caller cannot fix this by retrying.
outcomes.notes: Not new in v0.9.7: the same reject existed in v0.9.5 (src/plugins/mesh/outbound_registry.rs:643/531, sha 20e7603) but was not catalogued in ferrum-edge-0.9.5. v0.9.7 change (PR #5595): requests stamped with the Inbound mesh direction are never enforced, even for unscoped operator-managed instances or when an inbound listener shares the outbound capture port number; v0.9.5 could return this reject for such inbound traffic. Runs in on_request_received (before auth). Status configurable 400-599 (plugin reject_status; mesh FERRUM_MESH_OUTBOUND_REGISTRY_REJECT_STATUS, default 502). Nothing was sent upstream.

outcomes.remediation: Caller: send the MCP request as plain UTF-8 JSON (no charset parameter, or charset=utf-8), without a byte-order mark, comments or other non-standard JSON, and without a content encoding; operator can confirm the reason in the transaction metadata (ai_shield_rejected).

For the two new reasons warn mode forwards the request and records ai_shield_warnings=<reason> (no client signal); the content-encoding refusal applies in warn mode too. ai_prompt_shield (priority 2925) runs before mcp_gateway (2992): for the same non-UTF-8 charset an enforcing shield answers this 400, and mcp_gateway alone answers -32600 (plugin.mcp_gateway.invalid_request). Caller: use plain HTTP or gRPC-Web on this route if the API allows it.

outcomes.condition: A mesh HBONE CONNECT (TCP or UDP relay) that declares a native gRPC or gRPC-Web Content-Type. Refused before routing; no tunnel is opened.

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The Ferrum mesh proxy refused an HBONE tunnel request because it declared a gRPC content type; gRPC must be carried inside the tunnel, not on the CONNECT itself.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the destination is unreachable or that mesh policy denied the peer.

outcomes.condition: A sidecar mesh-mTLS, HBONE or Unix-socket dispatch is still waiting for backend response headers when the client's upload turns out malformed or incomplete without proof that the client left (for example an early EOF from a client that half-closed its side and is still reading).

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway ended the request because the client's request body was malformed or ended early before the backend answered; the backend was not blamed.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend failed or reset the exchange, or that the client disconnected.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: send a complete, well-framed body before half-closing the connection.

The BackendResponse is built with an empty header map, so Content-Type was not confirmed; it may be set by the final response builder (not traced). HTTP/3 logs the same 400 with rejection phase invalid_h3_upload. Mesh-only dispatchers: the mesh slice may prefer to own this entry.

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: If the response came from a Ferrum Edge gateway, its request_deduplication plugin refused the request because it could not decode the Brotli request body to fingerprint it (malformed, or larger than its decode limit); nothing was sent upstream.

outcomes.notes: New in v0.9.15; earlier releases decoded Brotli with an uncharged decoder and fingerprinted the original bytes when decoding failed. Public reason detail: malformed and over-limit collapse. Distinguishability: unique body.

error_class_semantics_note: request_reached_wire below records the unchanged retry::request_reached_wire(ErrorClass) classification defaults, not proof of actual backend handoff. Terminal gateway policy, client cancellation and authorization expiry can retain conservative class defaults. In v0.9.11 BackendResponse.request_on_wire (src/retry.rs:1906) independently carries handoff state; authorization refusals are health-neutral before and after transmission. Public markers cannot infer that internal state. v0.9.14 (#6019, #6022): a backend HTTP/2 RST_STREAM or GOAWAY with any reason except NO_ERROR, before response headers on a reqwest route, during a buffered body read, or while a direct-H2/gRPC body streams, is protocol_error (was request_error) and is charged to circuit breakers and passive health (src/retry.rs:1669 is_backend_h2_reset); a reset the gateway raises itself is not. Buffered-collector read errors report their real class instead of response_body_too_large. No class, token, status or request_reached_wire default changed; these are operator-visible classifications, not public signals. v0.9.15 leaves src/retry.rs byte-identical: no class, token, status or request_reached_wire default changed, and the new route_protocol_admission refusal maps to no token. v0.9.17 (#6127) adds the loop_detected token and never retries a backend 508; v0.9.19 changes client-visible statuses for connection_timeout (504) and backend_connection_limit (503) without changing request_reached_wire.
